    22 |     "delta_io",
    23 |     "delta_buffer_reads",
    24 | )
    25 | 
    26 | FEATURE_NAMES = (
    27 |     "baseline_latency",
    28 |     "baseline_p95",
    29 |     "baseline_cpu",
    30 |     "baseline_io",
    31 |     "baseline_buffer_reads",
    32 |     "baseline_buffer_hits",
    33 |     "baseline_rows",
    34 |     "baseline_calls",
    35 |     "baseline_selectivity",
    36 |     "table_size_bytes",
    37 |     "index_size_bytes",
    38 |     "dead_tuple_ratio",
    39 |     "idx_scan_ratio",
    40 |     "cardinality_error",
    41 |     "plan_cost",
    42 |     "plan_actual_time",
    43 |     "plan_buffer_reads",
    44 |     "query_frequency",
    45 |     "candidate_is_create_index",
    46 |     "candidate_is_drop_index",
    47 |     "candidate_is_analyze",
    48 |     "candidate_is_rewrite",
    49 |     "candidate_is_config",
    50 |     "candidate_sql_length",
    51 |     "candidate_has_where",
    52 |     "candidate_has_join",
    53 |     "candidate_column_count",
    54 |     "candidate_is_partial",
    55 |     "candidate_selectivity",
    56 |     "candidate_stats_target",
    57 | )
    58 | 
    59 | OUTCOME_LABELS = ("GOOD", "BAD", "NEUTRAL", "REGRESSION")
    60 | _NUMBER = re.compile(r"[-+]?\d+(?:\.\d+)?")
    61 | 
    62 | 
    63 | def _mapping(row: Mapping[str, Any], name: str) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
    64 |     value = row.get(name)
    65 |     return value if isinstance(value, Mapping) else row
    66 | 
    67 | 
    68 | def _number(row: Mapping[str, Any], *names: str, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
    69 |     for name in names:
    70 |         value = row.get(name)
    71 |         if value is not None:
    72 |             try:
    73 |                 return float(value)
    74 |             except (TypeError, ValueError):
    75 |                 continue
    76 |     return default
    77 | 
    78 | 
    79 | def _baseline(row: Mapping[str, Any], name: str, *aliases: str) -> float:
    80 |     source = _mapping(row, "baseline")
    81 |     return _number(source, name, *aliases, f"baseline_{name}")
    82 | 
    83 | 
    84 | def _candidate(row: Mapping[str, Any], name: str, *aliases: str) -> float:
    85 |     source = _mapping(row, "candidate")
    86 |     return _number(source, name, *aliases, f"candidate_{name}")
    87 | 
    88 | 
    89 | def extract_features(row: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, float]:
    90 |     """Normalize one experiment/lab row into the stable numeric feature vector."""
    91 |     candidate = _mapping(row, "candidate")
    92 |     sql = str(row.get("candidate_sql", row.get("sql", candidate.get("candidate_sql", candidate.get("sql", "")))) or "")
    93 |     strategy = str(row.get("strategy", row.get("candidate_type", candidate.get("strategy", candidate.get("type", "")))) or "").upper()
    94 |     table_size = _number(row, "table_size_bytes", "table_size", "table_size_mb")
    95 |     if "table_size_mb" in row and "table_size_bytes" not in row:
    96 |         table_size *= 1024 * 1024
    97 |     baseline_latency = _baseline(row, "latency", "mean_latency", "execution_time")
    98 |     baseline_p95 = _baseline(row, "p95", "latency_p95", "p95_latency")
    99 |     baseline_cpu = _baseline(row, "cpu", "cpu_time")
   100 |     baseline_io = _baseline(row, "io", "io_bytes", "read_bytes")
   101 |     baseline_buffer_reads = _baseline(row, "buffer_reads", "shared_blks_read")
   102 |     baseline_buffer_hits = _baseline(row, "buffer_hits", "shared_blks_hit")
   103 |     return {
   104 |         "baseline_latency": baseline_latency,
   105 |         "baseline_p95": baseline_p95,
   106 |         "baseline_cpu": baseline_cpu,
   107 |         "baseline_io": baseline_io,
   108 |         "baseline_buffer_reads": baseline_buffer_reads,
   109 |         "baseline_buffer_hits": baseline_buffer_hits,
   110 |         "baseline_rows": _baseline(row, "rows", "actual_rows"),
   111 |         "baseline_calls": _baseline(row, "calls", "query_calls"),
   112 |         "baseline_selectivity": _number(row, "baseline_selectivity", "selectivity"),
   113 |         "table_size_bytes": table_size,
   114 |         "index_size_bytes": _number(row, "index_size_bytes", "index_size"),
   115 |         "dead_tuple_ratio": _number(row, "dead_tuple_ratio"),
   116 |         "idx_scan_ratio": _number(row, "idx_scan_ratio"),
   117 |         "cardinality_error": _number(row, "cardinality_error"),
   118 |         "plan_cost": _number(row, "plan_cost", "estimated_cost"),
   119 |         "plan_actual_time": _number(row, "plan_actual_time", "actual_time"),
   120 |         "plan_buffer_reads": _number(row, "plan_buffer_reads", "buffer_reads"),
   121 |         "query_frequency": _number(row, "query_frequency", "qps", "frequency"),
   122 |         "candidate_is_create_index": float(strategy in {"CREATE_INDEX", "CREATE INDEX"} or "CREATE INDEX" in sql.upper()),
   123 |         "candidate_is_drop_index": float(strategy in {"DROP_INDEX", "DROP INDEX"} or "DROP INDEX" in sql.upper()),
   124 |         "candidate_is_analyze": float(strategy == "ANALYZE" or re.search(r"\bANALYZE\b", sql, re.I) is not None),
   125 |         "candidate_is_rewrite": float(strategy in {"REWRITE", "QUERY_REWRITE"}),
   126 |         "candidate_is_config": float(strategy in {"CONFIG", "CONFIGURATION"}),
   127 |         "candidate_sql_length": float(len(sql)),
   128 |         "candidate_has_where": float(re.search(r"\bWHERE\b", sql, re.I) is not None),
   129 |         "candidate_has_join": float(re.search(r"\bJOIN\b", sql, re.I) is not None),
   130 |         "candidate_column_count": float(len(re.findall(r"[,()]", sql)) + 1 if sql else 0),
   131 |         "candidate_is_partial": float("WHERE" in sql.upper() and strategy in {"CREATE_INDEX", "CREATE INDEX"}),
   132 |         "candidate_selectivity": _number(row, "candidate_selectivity", "index_selectivity"),
   133 |         "candidate_stats_target": _number(row, "candidate_stats_target", "statistics_target"),
   134 |     }
   135 | 
   136 | 
   137 | def build_feature_matrix(rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> np.ndarray:
   138 |     return np.asarray([[extract_features(row)[name] for name in FEATURE_NAMES] for row in rows], dtype=np.float32)
   139 | 
   140 | 
   141 | def _target_value(row: Mapping[str, Any], target: str) -> float:
   142 |     explicit = row.get(target)
   143 |     if explicit is None:
   144 |         explicit = row.get({
   145 |             "delta_latency": "actual_latency_delta",
   146 |             "delta_p95": "actual_p95_delta",
   147 |             "delta_cpu": "actual_cpu_delta",
   148 |             "delta_io": "actual_io_delta",
   149 |             "delta_buffer_reads": "actual_buffer_reads_delta",
   150 |         }[target])
   151 |     if explicit is not None:
   152 |         return float(explicit)
   153 |     metric = target.removeprefix("delta_")
   154 |     return _candidate(row, metric, f"candidate_{metric}") - _baseline(row, metric, f"baseline_{metric}")
   155 | 
   156 | 
   157 | def build_target_matrix(rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> np.ndarray:
   158 |     return np.asarray([[_target_value(row, target) for target in TARGET_NAMES] for row in rows], dtype=np.float32)
   159 | 
   160 | 
   161 | def outcome_label(row: Mapping[str, Any], deltas: Mapping[str, float] | None = None) -> str:
   162 |     explicit = str(row.get("outcome_label", row.get("label", row.get("outcome", ""))) or "").upper()
   163 |     if explicit in OUTCOME_LABELS:
   164 |         return explicit
   165 |     values = deltas or {target: _target_value(row, target) for target in TARGET_NAMES}
   166 |     baseline = abs(_baseline(row, "latency", "mean_latency", "execution_time"))
   167 |     latency_delta = float(values.get("delta_latency", 0.0))
   168 |     threshold = max(baseline * 0.05, 1e-6)
   169 |     if latency_delta < -threshold:
   170 |         return "GOOD"
   171 |     if latency_delta > threshold * 2:
   172 |         return "REGRESSION"
   173 |     if latency_delta > threshold:
   174 |         return "BAD"
   175 |     return "NEUTRAL"

1 | """Inference for the Feature 2 query-performance delta predictor."""
     2 | 
     3 | from __future__ import annotations
     4 | 
     5 | import os
     6 | from collections.abc import Mapping
     7 | from pathlib import Path
     8 | from typing import Any
     9 | 
    10 | import joblib
    11 | import numpy as np
    12 | 
    13 | from app.ml.delta_predictor.features import TARGET_NAMES, build_feature_matrix, outcome_label
    14 | 
    15 | 
    16 | def _load(path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    17 |     return joblib.load(Path(path or os.getenv("DELTA_MODEL_PATH", "delta_predictor.joblib")))
    18 | 
    19 | 
    20 | def predict(row: Mapping[str, Any], model_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, *, z_value: float = 1.96) -> dict[str, Any]:
    21 |     """Return all target deltas with bootstrap uncertainty intervals."""
    22 |     if z_value <= 0:
    23 |         raise ValueError("z_value must be positive")
    24 |     artifact = _load(model_path)
    25 |     values = build_feature_matrix([row])
    26 |     estimates: dict[str, float] = {}
    27 |     intervals: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    28 |     target_confidence: dict[str, float] = {}
    29 |     residual_scales = np.asarray(artifact.get("residual_scales", np.zeros(len(TARGET_NAMES))), dtype=float)
    30 |     for index, target in enumerate(artifact.get("target_names", TARGET_NAMES)):
    31 |         members = np.asarray([float(model.predict(values)[0]) for model in artifact["models"][index]], dtype=float)
    32 |         estimate = float(np.mean(members))
    33 |         ensemble_variance = np.var(members, ddof=1) if len(members) > 1 else 0.0
    34 |         uncertainty = float(np.sqrt(ensemble_variance + residual_scales[index] ** 2))
    35 |         # A lower/upper interval is conservative: it includes model spread and
    36 |         # the observed training residual scale.
    37 |         half_width = z_value * uncertainty
    38 |         lower, upper = estimate - half_width, estimate + half_width
    39 |         confidence = float(np.clip(1.0 / (1.0 + half_width / max(abs(estimate), residual_scales[index], 1e-6)), 0.0, 1.0))
    40 |         estimates[target] = estimate
    41 |         intervals[target] = {"estimate": estimate, "lower": float(lower), "upper": float(upper), "confidence": confidence}
    42 |         target_confidence[target] = confidence
    43 |     label = outcome_label(row, estimates)
    44 |     return {
    45 |         "deltas": estimates,
    46 |         "predictions": intervals,
    47 |         "confidence_intervals": {target: {key: value for key, value in interval.items() if key in {"lower", "upper"}} for target, interval in intervals.items()},
    48 |         "confidence": float(np.mean(list(target_confidence.values()))),
    49 |         "target_confidence": target_confidence,
    50 |         "outcome_label": label,
    51 |         "model_version": artifact.get("model_version", "unknown"),
    52 |     }

chunk_177c6060104e847e.numbered_code:
1 | """Train the LightGBM query-performance delta predictor."""
     2 | 
     3 | from __future__ import annotations
     4 | 
     5 | import os
     6 | from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
     7 | from pathlib import Path
     8 | from typing import Any
     9 | 
    10 | import joblib
    11 | import numpy as np
    12 | from lightgbm import LGBMRegressor
    13 | from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error, r2_score
    14 | 
    15 | from app.ml.delta_predictor.features import FEATURE_NAMES, TARGET_NAMES, build_feature_matrix, build_target_matrix, outcome_label
    16 | 
    17 | 
    18 | class ConstantRegressor:
    19 |     """Pickleable fallback for a target with insufficient variation."""
    20 | 
    21 |     def __init__(self, value: float = 0.0) -> None:
    22 |         self.value = float(value)
    23 | 
    24 |     def predict(self, values: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    25 |         return np.full(len(values), self.value, dtype=float)
    26 | 
    27 | 
    28 | def _fit_ensemble(values: np.ndarray, target: np.ndarray, *, random_state: int, members: int) -> list[Any]:
    29 |     models: list[Any] = []
    30 |     rng = np.random.default_rng(random_state)
    31 |     for member in range(members):
    32 |         indices = rng.integers(0, len(values), size=len(values))
    33 |         if np.ptp(target[indices]) < 1e-12:
    34 |             models.append(ConstantRegressor(float(np.mean(target[indices]))))
    35 |             continue
    36 |         models.append(LGBMRegressor(
    37 |             n_estimators=120,
    38 |             learning_rate=0.04,
    39 |             num_leaves=min(15, max(3, len(values) // 3)),
    40 |             max_depth=5,
    41 |             min_child_samples=max(3, min(20, len(values) // 5)),
    42 |             reg_lambda=0.2,
    43 |             verbosity=-1,
    44 |             random_state=random_state + member,
    45 |         ).fit(values[indices], target[indices]))
    46 |     return models
    47 | 
    48 | 
    49 | def _metrics(actual: np.ndarray, predicted: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
    50 |     result = {
    51 |         "mae": float(mean_absolute_error(actual, predicted)),
    52 |         "rmse": float(np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(actual, predicted))),
    53 |     }
    54 |     result["r2"] = float(r2_score(actual, predicted)) if np.ptp(actual) > 1e-12 else 0.0
    55 |     return result
    56 | 
    57 | 
    58 | def train(
    59 |     rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    60 |     artifact_path: str | os.PathLike[str] = "delta_predictor.joblib",
    61 |     *,
    62 |     random_state: int = 42,
    63 |     ensemble_size: int = 7,
    64 |     validation_fraction: float = 0.2,
    65 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    66 |     """Fit and persist an ensemble using a temporal holdout for validation."""
    67 |     if len(rows) < 8:
    68 |         raise ValueError("At least eight chronological experiment rows are required")
    69 |     if not 0.1 <= validation_fraction < 0.5:
    70 |         raise ValueError("validation_fraction must be between 0.1 and 0.5")
    71 |     if ensemble_size < 3:
    72 |         raise ValueError("ensemble_size must be at least 3")
    73 |     values = build_feature_matrix(rows)
    74 |     targets = build_target_matrix(rows)
    75 |     split = min(len(rows) - 2, max(2, int(len(rows) * (1 - validation_fraction))))
    76 |     train_values, valid_values = values[:split], values[split:]
    77 |     train_targets, valid_targets = targets[:split], targets[split:]
    78 |     validation_models = [_fit_ensemble(train_values, train_targets[:, index], random_state=random_state + index * 101, members=ensemble_size) for index in range(len(TARGET_NAMES))]
    79 |     validation_predictions = np.column_stack([np.mean([model.predict(valid_values) for model in models], axis=0) for models in validation_models])
    80 |     validation_metrics = {target: _metrics(valid_targets[:, index], validation_predictions[:, index]) for index, target in enumerate(TARGET_NAMES)}
    81 | 
    82 |     models = [_fit_ensemble(values, targets[:, index], random_state=random_state + index * 101, members=ensemble_size) for index in range(len(TARGET_NAMES))]
    83 |     residual_scales = np.std(targets - np.column_stack([np.mean([model.predict(values) for model in target_models], axis=0) for target_models in models]), axis=0, ddof=1)
    84 |     artifact = {
    85 |         "models": models,
    86 |         "feature_names": FEATURE_NAMES,
    87 |         "target_names": TARGET_NAMES,
    88 |         "residual_scales": np.nan_to_num(residual_scales, nan=0.0),
    89 |         "model_version": "delta-lgbm-ensemble-v1",
    90 |         "validation_metrics": validation_metrics,
    91 |         "outcome_labels": sorted({outcome_label(row) for row in rows}),
    92 |     }
    93 |     path = Path(artifact_path)
    94 |     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    95 |     joblib.dump(artifact, path)
    96 |     _log_mlflow(path, len(rows), split, validation_metrics)
    97 |     return {"artifact_path": str(path), "rows": len(rows), "feature_names": list(FEATURE_NAMES), "targets": list(TARGET_NAMES), "validation_metrics": validation_metrics}
    98 | 
    99 | 
   100 | def _log_mlflow(path: Path, row_count: int, split: int, metrics: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, float]]) -> None:
   101 |     try:
   102 |         import mlflow
   103 | 
   104 |         mlflow.set_tracking_uri(os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI", "http://localhost:5000"))
   105 |         with mlflow.start_run(run_name="delta-predictor-lightgbm"):
   106 |             mlflow.log_params({"rows": row_count, "temporal_train_rows": split, "targets": len(TARGET_NAMES)})
   107 |             mlflow.log_metrics({f"{target}_{name}": value for target, values in metrics.items() for name, value in values.items()})
   108 |             mlflow.log_artifact(str(path), artifact_path="model")
   109 |     except Exception:
   110 |         return
   111 | 
   112 | 
   113 | if __name__ == "__main__":
   114 |     raise SystemExit("Import train() and provide optimization experiment rows")

1 | """Resolve promoted, real-data Feature 1 model artifacts.
     2 | 
     3 | Live diagnosis must never manufacture training data. Model artifacts are
     4 | deployment inputs; missing artifacts are reported explicitly to the caller.
     5 | """
     6 | 
     7 | from __future__ import annotations
     8 | 
     9 | import os
    10 | import json
    11 | from pathlib import Path
    12 | from typing import Any
    13 | 
    14 | from app.core.config import get_settings
    15 | 
    16 | 
    17 | def _artifact_path(environment_name: str, default_name: str) -> Path:
    18 |     settings = get_settings()
    19 |     configured = os.getenv(environment_name) or getattr(settings, environment_name, None)
    20 |     path = Path(configured or default_name)
    21 |     if not path.is_absolute():
    22 |         path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / path
    23 |     return path
    24 | 
    25 | 
    26 | def model_paths() -> dict[str, Path]:
    27 |     return {
    28 |         "anomaly": _artifact_path("ANOMALY_MODEL_PATH", ".artifacts/anomaly_model.joblib"),
    29 |         "rca": _artifact_path("RCA_MODEL_PATH", ".artifacts/rca_model.joblib"),
    30 |         "temporal": _artifact_path("TEMPORAL_MODEL_PATH", ".artifacts/temporal_model.pt"),
    31 |         "manifest": _artifact_path("FEATURE1_MANIFEST_PATH", ".artifacts/manifest.json"),
    32 |     }
    33 | 
    34 | 
    35 | def ensure_feature1_models() -> dict[str, Any]:
    36 |     """Describe deployed model artifacts without creating replacement data."""
    37 |     paths = model_paths()
    38 |     missing = [name for name, path in paths.items() if not path.is_file()]
    39 |     manifest: dict[str, Any] = {}
    40 |     if not missing:
    41 |         try:
    42 |             manifest = json.loads(paths["manifest"].read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    43 |             if manifest.get("source") != "fault_lab" or manifest.get("status") != "promoted":
    44 |                 missing.append("manifest")
    45 |         except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):

    47 |     return {
    48 |         "status": "ready" if not missing else "missing_artifact",
    49 |         "source": manifest.get("source") if not missing else "none",
    50 |         "missing": missing,
    51 |         "paths": {name: str(path) for name, path in paths.items()},
    52 |         "manifest": manifest if not missing else None,
    53 |     }

chunk_367a8eff05c7b8be.numbered_code:
1 | """Feature 3 L1 Workload & Resource Degradation Forecasting Feature Engineering.
     2 | 
     3 | Constructs multi-resolution time-series features (1h–168h lags, rolling window
     4 | aggregates, growth rates, acceleration, table/index metrics, and calendar features)
     5 | for LightGBM forecasting with conformal calibration.
     6 | 
     7 | Reference: ARCHITECTURE.md §4, §8 & PRD.md §5 Feature 3 L1.
     8 | """
     9 | 
    10 | from __future__ import annotations
    11 | 
    12 | import math
    13 | from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
    14 | from datetime import datetime, timezone
    15 | from typing import Any
    16 | 
    17 | import numpy as np
    18 | 
    19 | LAG_HOURS = [1, 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 72, 168]
    20 | ROLLING_WINDOWS = [6, 24, 72, 168]
    21 | 
    22 | BASE_METRIC_NAMES = [
    23 |     "mean_exec_time",
    24 |     "max_exec_time",
    25 |     "p95_exec_time",
    26 |     "calls",
    27 |     "rows",
    28 |     "shared_blks_read",
    29 |     "shared_blks_hit",
    30 |     "temp_blks_read",
    31 |     "temp_blks_written",
    32 |     "cpu_seconds",
    33 |     "wal_bytes",
    34 |     "dead_tuple_ratio",
    35 |     "table_size_bytes",
    36 |     "index_size_bytes",
    37 |     "idx_scan_ratio",
    38 | ]
    39 | 
    40 | 
    41 | def _feature_names() -> list[str]:
    42 |     names: list[str] = []
    43 |     # Base snapshot metrics
    44 |     names.extend([f"current_{m}" for m in BASE_METRIC_NAMES])
    45 |     # Lags
    46 |     for lag in LAG_HOURS:
    47 |         names.extend([f"lag_{lag}h_{m}" for m in ["mean_exec_time", "p95_exec_time", "calls", "cpu_seconds", "shared_blks_read"]])
    48 |     # Rolling aggregates (mean, std, max, growth)
    49 |     for window in ROLLING_WINDOWS:
    50 |         names.extend([
    51 |             f"roll_{window}h_mean_p95",
    52 |             f"roll_{window}h_std_p95",
    53 |             f"roll_{window}h_max_p95",
    54 |             f"roll_{window}h_mean_calls",
    55 |             f"roll_{window}h_growth_rate",
    56 |         ])
    57 |     # Growth & acceleration deltas
    58 |     names.extend([
    59 |         "growth_1h_p95",
    60 |         "growth_24h_p95",
    61 |         "growth_168h_p95",
    62 |         "acceleration_p95",
    63 |         "io_intensity_ratio",
    64 |         "cache_hit_ratio",
    65 |     ])
    66 |     # Calendar features
    67 |     names.extend([
    68 |         "hour_sin",
    69 |         "hour_cos",
    70 |         "day_of_week_sin",
    71 |         "day_of_week_cos",
    72 |         "is_weekend",
    73 |     ])
    74 |     return names
    75 | 
    76 | 
    77 | FEATURE_NAMES: list[str] = _feature_names()
    78 | 
    79 | 
    80 | def extract_calendar_features(dt: datetime | None) -> dict[str, float]:
    81 |     """Extract cyclical calendar features from a timestamp."""
    82 |     if dt is None:
    83 |         dt = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    84 |     hour = dt.hour + dt.minute / 60.0
    85 |     day = dt.weekday() + hour / 24.0
    86 | 
    87 |     return {
    88 |         "hour_sin": math.sin(2.0 * math.pi * hour / 24.0),
    89 |         "hour_cos": math.cos(2.0 * math.pi * hour / 24.0),
    90 |         "day_of_week_sin": math.sin(2.0 * math.pi * day / 7.0),
    91 |         "day_of_week_cos": math.cos(2.0 * math.pi * day / 7.0),
    92 |         "is_weekend": 1.0 if dt.weekday() >= 5 else 0.0,
    93 |     }
    94 | 
    95 | 
    96 | def extract_telemetry_features(
    97 |     history: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    98 |     current_time: datetime | None = None,
    99 | ) -> dict[str, float]:
   100 |     """Extract full L1 feature vector from a chronological telemetry history sequence.
   101 | 
   102 |     `history` should be a sequence of telemetry snapshots sorted in ascending chronological order.
   103 |     """
   104 |     features: dict[str, float] = {name: 0.0 for name in FEATURE_NAMES}
   105 |     if not history:
   106 |         calendar = extract_calendar_features(current_time)
   107 |         features.update(calendar)
   108 |         return features
   109 | 
   110 |     latest = history[-1]
   111 |     ts_latest = latest.get("timestamp")
   112 |     if isinstance(ts_latest, str):
   113 |         try:
   114 |             ts_latest = datetime.fromisoformat(ts_latest.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
   115 |         except Exception:
   116 |             ts_latest = current_time or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   117 |     elif not isinstance(ts_latest, datetime):
   118 |         ts_latest = current_time or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   119 | 
   120 |     # 1. Base snapshot metrics
   121 |     for m in BASE_METRIC_NAMES:
   122 |         val = latest.get(m, latest.get(f"avg_{m}", 0.0))
   123 |         features[f"current_{m}"] = float(val) if val is not None else 0.0
   124 | 
   125 |     # 2. Extract series for lag and rolling features
   126 |     p95_series = [float(h.get("p95_exec_time", h.get("max_exec_time", h.get("mean_exec_time", 0.0)))) for h in history]
   127 |     calls_series = [float(h.get("calls", 1.0)) for h in history]
   128 |     mean_series = [float(h.get("mean_exec_time", 0.0)) for h in history]
   129 |     cpu_series = [float(h.get("cpu_seconds", 0.0)) for h in history]
   130 |     io_series = [float(h.get("shared_blks_read", 0.0)) for h in history]
   131 | 
   132 |     n_points = len(history)
   133 | 
   134 |     # 3. Lags
   135 |     for lag in LAG_HOURS:
   136 |         idx = max(0, n_points - 1 - lag)
   137 |         lag_entry = history[idx] if idx < n_points else latest
   138 |         features[f"lag_{lag}h_mean_exec_time"] = float(lag_entry.get("mean_exec_time", 0.0))
   139 |         features[f"lag_{lag}h_p95_exec_time"] = float(lag_entry.get("p95_exec_time", lag_entry.get("max_exec_time", 0.0)))
   140 |         features[f"lag_{lag}h_calls"] = float(lag_entry.get("calls", 0.0))
   141 |         features[f"lag_{lag}h_cpu_seconds"] = float(lag_entry.get("cpu_seconds", 0.0))
   142 |         features[f"lag_{lag}h_shared_blks_read"] = float(lag_entry.get("shared_blks_read", 0.0))
   143 | 
   144 |     # 4. Rolling aggregates
   145 |     for window in ROLLING_WINDOWS:
   146 |         sub_p95 = p95_series[-window:] if len(p95_series) >= window else p95_series
   147 |         sub_calls = calls_series[-window:] if len(calls_series) >= window else calls_series
   148 | 
   149 |         mean_val = float(np.mean(sub_p95)) if sub_p95 else 0.0
   150 |         std_val = float(np.std(sub_p95)) if len(sub_p95) > 1 else 0.0
   151 |         max_val = float(np.max(sub_p95)) if sub_p95 else 0.0
   152 |         mean_calls = float(np.mean(sub_calls)) if sub_calls else 0.0
   153 | 
   154 |         growth = (sub_p95[-1] - sub_p95[0]) / max(sub_p95[0], 1e-6) if len(sub_p95) >= 2 else 0.0
   155 | 
   156 |         features[f"roll_{window}h_mean_p95"] = mean_val
   157 |         features[f"roll_{window}h_std_p95"] = std_val
   158 |         features[f"roll_{window}h_max_p95"] = max_val
   159 |         features[f"roll_{window}h_mean_calls"] = mean_calls
   160 |         features[f"roll_{window}h_growth_rate"] = growth
   161 | 
   162 |     # 5. Growth deltas and acceleration
   163 |     curr_p95 = p95_series[-1] if p95_series else 0.0
   164 |     p95_1h = p95_series[-2] if len(p95_series) >= 2 else curr_p95
   165 |     p95_24h = p95_series[-25] if len(p95_series) >= 25 else p95_series[0]
   166 |     p95_168h = p95_series[-169] if len(p95_series) >= 169 else p95_series[0]
   167 | 
   168 |     g1 = (curr_p95 - p95_1h) / max(p95_1h, 1e-6)
   169 |     g24 = (curr_p95 - p95_24h) / max(p95_24h, 1e-6)
   170 |     g168 = (curr_p95 - p95_168h) / max(p95_168h, 1e-6)
   171 | 
   172 |     features["growth_1h_p95"] = g1
   173 |     features["growth_24h_p95"] = g24
   174 |     features["growth_168h_p95"] = g168
   175 |     features["acceleration_p95"] = g1 - (g24 / 24.0)
   176 | 
   177 |     # 6. Interaction ratios
   178 |     reads = float(latest.get("shared_blks_read", 0.0))
   179 |     hits = float(latest.get("shared_blks_hit", 0.0))
   180 |     features["cache_hit_ratio"] = hits / max(hits + reads, 1.0)
   181 |     features["io_intensity_ratio"] = reads / max(float(latest.get("calls", 1.0)), 1.0)
   182 | 
   183 |     # 7. Calendar
   184 |     calendar = extract_calendar_features(ts_latest)
   185 |     features.update(calendar)
   186 | 
   187 |     return features
   188 | 
   189 | 
   190 | def build_feature_matrix(rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> np.ndarray:
   191 |     """Build numeric feature matrix from extracted feature dictionaries."""
   192 |     matrix = np.zeros((len(rows), len(FEATURE_NAMES)), dtype=np.float32)
   193 |     for i, row in enumerate(rows):
   194 |         for j, name in enumerate(FEATURE_NAMES):
   195 |             val = row.get(name, 0.0)
   196 |             matrix[i, j] = float(val) if val is not None and not math.isnan(float(val)) else 0.0
   197 |     return matrix

1 | """Feature 3 L1 Workload Degradation Forecasting Inference.
     2 | 
     3 | Generates multi-step degradation probability curves (degradation_probability(t))
     4 | and conformal confidence intervals from input telemetry history.
     5 | 
     6 | Reference: ARCHITECTURE.md §4, §8 & PRD.md §5 Feature 3 L1.
     7 | """
     8 | 
     9 | from __future__ import annotations
    10 | 
    11 | import os
    12 | from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
    13 | from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
    14 | from pathlib import Path
    15 | from typing import Any
    16 | 
    17 | import joblib
    18 | import numpy as np
    19 | 
    20 | from app.core.logging import get_logger
    21 | from app.ml.forecasting.features import FEATURE_NAMES, build_feature_matrix, extract_telemetry_features
    22 | 
    23 | logger = get_logger(__name__)

    25 | 
    26 | def _load_model(model_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    27 |     """Load serialized L1 forecasting artifact."""
    28 |     target_path = Path(model_path or os.getenv("FORECASTING_MODEL_PATH", "forecasting_model.joblib"))
    29 |     if not target_path.exists():
    30 |         return None
    31 |     try:
    32 |         return joblib.load(target_path)
    33 |     except Exception as exc:
    34 |         logger.warning(f"Failed to load forecasting artifact at {target_path}: {exc}")
    35 |         return None
    36 | 
    37 | 
    38 | def _sigmoid(x: float) -> float:
    39 |     return float(1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(x, -20.0, 20.0))))
    40 | 
    41 | 
    42 | def predict(
    43 |     telemetry_history: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    44 |     horizon_hours: int = 168,  # Default 7 days (168h) per PRD §5
    45 |     model_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    46 |     current_time: datetime | None = None,
    47 |     action_threshold: float = 0.40,
    48 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    49 |     """Generate future degradation probability curve and conformal prediction intervals.
    50 | 
    51 |     Returns:
    52 |         Dict containing:
    53 |             - degradation_probability: scalar overall risk (0.0 to 1.0)
    54 |             - is_flagged_for_action: bool (True if degradation risk exceeds threshold)
    55 |             - probability_curve: list of hourly DegradationCurvePoint dicts
    56 |             - forecast_window_start / end: ISO timestamps
    57 |             - model_version: str
    58 |     """
    59 |     now = current_time or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    60 |     if telemetry_history:
    61 |         latest_ts = telemetry_history[-1].get("timestamp")
    62 |         if isinstance(latest_ts, datetime):
    63 |             now = latest_ts
    64 |         elif isinstance(latest_ts, str):
    65 |             try:
    66 |                 now = datetime.fromisoformat(latest_ts.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    67 |             except Exception:
    68 |                 pass
    69 | 
    70 |     window_start = now
    71 |     window_end = now + timedelta(hours=horizon_hours)
    72 | 
    73 |     features = extract_telemetry_features(telemetry_history, current_time=now)
    74 |     X = build_feature_matrix([features])
    75 | 
    76 |     artifact = _load_model(model_path)
    77 | 
    78 |     if artifact is not None and "model" in artifact:
    79 |         model = artifact["model"]
    80 |         q_conformal = float(artifact.get("q_conformal", 0.15))
    81 |         version = str(artifact.get("version", "l1_v1"))
    82 | 
    83 |         # Base 24h delta prediction
    84 |         base_delta = float(model.predict(X)[0])
    85 |     else:
    86 |         # Heuristic statistical fallback for cold start before first model train
    87 |         p95_growth = float(features.get("growth_24h_p95", 0.0))
    88 |         dead_tuple_ratio = float(features.get("current_dead_tuple_ratio", 0.05))
    89 |         base_delta = p95_growth * 1.5 + dead_tuple_ratio * 0.5
    90 |         q_conformal = 0.20
    91 |         version = "heuristic_v0"
    92 | 
    93 |     # Project degradation probability curve over horizon hours
    94 |     curve: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    95 |     max_prob = 0.0
    96 | 
    97 |     # Hourly or multi-hour step progression
    98 |     step_hours = 6 if horizon_hours > 48 else 1
    99 |     for h in range(1, horizon_hours + 1, step_hours):
   100 |         t_point = window_start + timedelta(hours=h)
   101 | 
   102 |         # Time-scaling: compounding effect over horizon
   103 |         time_factor = (h / 24.0) ** 0.8
   104 |         projected_delta = base_delta * (1.0 + 0.05 * time_factor)
   105 | 
   106 |         # Conformal prediction interval
   107 |         lower_delta = projected_delta - q_conformal
   108 |         upper_delta = projected_delta + q_conformal
   109 | 
   110 |         # Map delta to probability of degradation (> 20% latency increase)
   111 |         point_prob = _sigmoid((projected_delta - 0.15) * 5.0)
   112 |         lower_prob = _sigmoid((lower_delta - 0.15) * 5.0)
   113 |         upper_prob = _sigmoid((upper_delta - 0.15) * 5.0)
   114 | 
   115 |         max_prob = max(max_prob, point_prob)
   116 | 
   117 |         curve.append({
   118 |             "timestamp": t_point.isoformat(),
   119 |             "predicted_probability": float(point_prob),
   120 |             "confidence_lower": float(lower_prob),
   121 |             "confidence_upper": float(upper_prob),
   122 |             "projected_delta_ratio": float(projected_delta),
   123 |         })
   124 | 
   125 |     is_flagged = bool(max_prob >= action_threshold)
   126 | 
   127 |     return {
   128 |         "degradation_probability": float(max_prob),
   129 |         "is_flagged_for_action": is_flagged,
   130 |         "forecast_window_start": window_start.isoformat(),
   131 |         "forecast_window_end": window_end.isoformat(),
   132 |         "probability_curve": curve,
   133 |         "model_version": version,
   134 |         "conformal_quantile": float(q_conformal),
   135 |     }

30 | def generate_synthetic_telemetry_series(
    31 |     n_days: int = 30,
    32 |     interval_hours: int = 1,
    33 |     degradation_start_day: int = 20,
    34 | ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    35 |     """Generate realistic synthetic time-series telemetry with diurnal cycles and end-of-period degradation."""
    36 |     import math
    37 |     from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
    38 | 
    39 |     records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    40 |     base_time = datetime(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    41 |     total_hours = n_days * 24
    42 | 
    43 |     np.random.seed(42)
    44 |     base_p95 = 50.0
    45 | 
    46 |     for step in range(0, total_hours, interval_hours):
    47 |         ts = base_time + timedelta(hours=step)
    48 |         hour = ts.hour
    49 |         is_peak = 9 <= hour <= 18
    50 |         traffic_mult = 2.0 if is_peak else 0.8
    51 | 
    52 |         day = step / 24.0
    53 |         # Degradation trend after degradation_start_day
    54 |         degradation_mult = 1.0 + (max(0.0, day - degradation_start_day) ** 1.3) * 0.15
    55 | 
    56 |         noise = np.random.normal(1.0, 0.05)
    57 |         p95 = float(base_p95 * traffic_mult * degradation_mult * noise)
    58 |         calls = float(1000 * traffic_mult * noise)
    59 |         cpu = float(0.2 * traffic_mult * degradation_mult * noise)
    60 |         shared_reads = float(500 * traffic_mult * degradation_mult * noise)
    61 |         shared_hits = float(10000 * traffic_mult * noise)
    62 | 
    63 |         records.append({
    64 |             "timestamp": ts.isoformat(),
    65 |             "mean_exec_time": p95 * 0.5,
    66 |             "max_exec_time": p95 * 1.5,
    67 |             "p95_exec_time": p95,
    68 |             "calls": calls,
    69 |             "rows": calls * 5,
    70 |             "cpu_seconds": cpu,
    71 |             "shared_blks_read": shared_reads,
    72 |             "shared_blks_hit": shared_hits,
    73 |             "temp_blks_read": 0.0,
    74 |             "temp_blks_written": 0.0,
    75 |             "wal_bytes": calls * 500.0,
    76 |             "dead_tuple_ratio": min(0.4, 0.02 + day * 0.01),
    77 |             "table_size_bytes": 100_000_000 + int(day * 5_000_000),
    78 |             "index_size_bytes": 20_000_000 + int(day * 1_000_000),
    79 |             "idx_scan_ratio": max(0.2, 0.9 - day * 0.02),
    80 |         })
    81 |     return records

82 | 
    83 | 
    84 | def build_forecasting_dataset(
    85 |     telemetry_records: Sequence[dict[str, Any]],
    86 |     horizon_steps: int = 24,  # e.g., forecast 24 hours into the future
    87 |     min_history_steps: int = 48,
    88 |     degradation_threshold_ratio: float = 0.25,  # 25% latency increase indicates degradation
    89 | ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, list[str]]:
    90 |     """Convert raw chronological telemetry into sliding-window feature rows and target deltas."""
    91 |     if len(telemetry_records) < (min_history_steps + horizon_steps):
    92 |         raise ValueError(
    93 |             f"Insufficient telemetry records ({len(telemetry_records)}). "
    94 |             f"Require at least {min_history_steps + horizon_steps} points."
    95 |         )
    96 | 
    97 |     feature_rows: list[dict[str, float]] = []
    98 |     y_reg_deltas: list[float] = []
    99 |     y_prob_targets: list[float] = []
   100 | 
   101 |     for t in range(min_history_steps, len(telemetry_records) - horizon_steps):
   102 |         window = telemetry_records[: t + 1]
   103 |         future_window = telemetry_records[t + 1 : t + 1 + horizon_steps]
   104 | 
   105 |         features = extract_telemetry_features(window)
   106 |         feature_rows.append(features)
   107 | 
   108 |         curr_p95 = float(window[-1].get("p95_exec_time", window[-1].get("mean_exec_time", 1.0)))
   109 |         future_p95_max = max(float(f.get("p95_exec_time", f.get("mean_exec_time", 1.0))) for f in future_window)
   110 | 
   111 |         # Delta ratio: (future - current) / current
   112 |         delta_ratio = (future_p95_max - curr_p95) / max(curr_p95, 1e-6)
   113 |         y_reg_deltas.append(delta_ratio)
   114 | 
   115 |         # Probability target: smooth sigmoid over threshold
   116 |         is_degraded = 1.0 if delta_ratio >= degradation_threshold_ratio else 0.0
   117 |         y_prob_targets.append(is_degraded)
   118 | 
   119 |     X = build_feature_matrix(feature_rows)
   120 |     y_reg = np.asarray(y_reg_deltas, dtype=np.float32)
   121 |     y_prob = np.asarray(y_prob_targets, dtype=np.float32)
   122 | 
   123 |     return X, y_reg, y_prob, FEATURE_NAMES

chunk_9201114efebb27e9.numbered_code:
124 | 
   125 | 
   126 | def walk_forward_train(
   127 |     X: np.ndarray,
   128 |     y: np.ndarray,
   129 |     n_splits: int = 4,
   130 |     min_train_ratio: float = 0.5,
   131 | ) -> tuple[lgb.LGBMRegressor, float, dict[str, float]]:
   132 |     """Perform walk-forward temporal cross-validation and compute conformal calibration quantile."""
   133 |     n_samples = len(X)
   134 |     split_size = int((n_samples * (1.0 - min_train_ratio)) / n_splits)
   135 | 
   136 |     fold_maes: list[float] = []
   137 |     fold_rmses: list[float] = []
   138 |     all_val_residuals: list[float] = []
   139 | 
   140 |     model: lgb.LGBMRegressor | None = None
   141 | 
   142 |     for fold in range(n_splits):
   143 |         train_end = int(n_samples * min_train_ratio) + fold * split_size
   144 |         val_end = min(n_samples, train_end + split_size)
   145 | 
   146 |         X_train, y_train = X[:train_end], y[:train_end]
   147 |         X_val, y_val = X[train_end:val_end], y[train_end:val_end]
   148 | 
   149 |         fold_model = lgb.LGBMRegressor(
   150 |             n_estimators=100,
   151 |             learning_rate=0.05,
   152 |             num_leaves=31,
   153 |             random_state=42 + fold,
   154 |             verbosity=-1,
   155 |         )
   156 |         fold_model.fit(X_train, y_train)
   157 | 
   158 |         preds = fold_model.predict(X_val)
   159 |         residuals = np.abs(y_val - preds)
   160 |         all_val_residuals.extend(residuals.tolist())
   161 | 
   162 |         fold_maes.append(float(mean_absolute_error(y_val, preds)))
   163 |         fold_rmses.append(float(np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_val, preds))))
   164 |         model = fold_model
   165 | 
   166 |     # Final fit on entire historical dataset
   167 |     final_model = lgb.LGBMRegressor(
   168 |         n_estimators=120,
   169 |         learning_rate=0.05,
   170 |         num_leaves=31,
   171 |         random_state=42,
   172 |         verbosity=-1,
   173 |     )
   174 |     final_model.fit(X, y)
   175 | 
   176 |     # Conformal non-conformity calibration: 90% confidence quantile
   177 |     coverage_level = 0.90
   178 |     if all_val_residuals:
   179 |         residuals_arr = np.asarray(all_val_residuals)
   180 |         q_conformal = float(np.quantile(residuals_arr, coverage_level))
   181 |         actual_coverage = float(np.mean(residuals_arr <= q_conformal))
   182 |     else:
   183 |         q_conformal = 0.15
   184 |         actual_coverage = 0.90
   185 | 
   186 |     metrics = {
   187 |         "mae": float(np.mean(fold_maes)) if fold_maes else 0.0,
   188 |         "rmse": float(np.mean(fold_rmses)) if fold_rmses else 0.0,
   189 |         "conformal_quantile_90": q_conformal,
   190 |         "conformal_coverage": actual_coverage,
   191 |     }
   192 | 
   193 |     return final_model, q_conformal, metrics

   196 | def train(
   197 |     telemetry_records: Sequence[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
   198 |     output_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
   199 |     version: str = "v1",

1 | """Ground-truth record and JSONL dataset writer for fault-lab runs."""
     2 | 
     3 | from __future__ import annotations
     4 | 
     5 | import json
     6 | import uuid
     7 | from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
     8 | from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
     9 | from datetime import datetime, timezone
    10 | from pathlib import Path
    11 | from typing import Any
    12 | 
    13 | 
    14 | def _utc_now() -> str:
    15 |     return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    16 | 
    17 | 
    18 | @dataclass
    19 | class GroundTruthRecord:
    20 |     """One labeled experiment in the format consumed by RCA training."""
    21 | 
    22 |     scenario: str
    23 |     labels: list[str]
    24 |     telemetry: list[dict[str, Any]]
    25 |     experiment_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    26 |     started_at: str = field(default_factory=_utc_now)
    27 |     ended_at: str | None = None
    28 |     workload: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    29 |     fault_parameters: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    30 |     success: bool = True
    31 |     schema_version: str = "fault-lab.v1"
    32 | 
    33 |     def finish(self, *, success: bool = True) -> None:
    34 |         self.ended_at = _utc_now()
    35 |         self.success = success
    36 | 
    37 |     def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    38 |         """Serialize a JSON-safe record while retaining trainer labels."""
    39 |         return asdict(self)
    40 | 
    41 | 
    42 | class GroundTruthRecorder:
    43 |     """Append records to JSONL or write a complete deterministic dataset."""
    44 | 
    45 |     def __init__(self, dataset_path: str | Path) -> None:
    46 |         self.dataset_path = Path(dataset_path)
    47 | 
    48 |     def record(
    49 |         self,
    50 |         *,
    51 |         scenario: str,
    52 |         labels: Sequence[str],
    53 |         telemetry: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    54 |         workload: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    55 |         fault_parameters: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    56 |         success: bool = True,
    57 |     ) -> GroundTruthRecord:
    58 |         record = GroundTruthRecord(
    59 |             scenario=scenario,
    60 |             labels=list(labels),
    61 |             telemetry=[dict(row) for row in telemetry],
    62 |             workload=dict(workload or {}),
    63 |             fault_parameters=dict(fault_parameters or {}),
    64 |             success=success,
    65 |         )
    66 |         record.finish(success=success)
    67 |         self.append(record)
    68 |         return record
    69 | 
    70 |     def append(self, record: GroundTruthRecord) -> None:
    71 |         self.dataset_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    72 |         with self.dataset_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
    73 |             stream.write(json.dumps(record.to_dict(), sort_keys=True, default=str) + "\n")
    74 | 
    75 |     def read(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    76 |         if not self.dataset_path.exists():
    77 |             return []
    78 |         with self.dataset_path.open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
    79 |             return [json.loads(line) for line in stream if line.strip()]
    80 | 
    81 | 
    82 | def flatten_records(records: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    83 |     """Expand each labeled record into RCA trainer rows."""
    84 |     rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    85 |     for record in records:
    86 |         for telemetry in record.get("telemetry", []):
    87 |             rows.append({**telemetry, "labels": list(record.get("labels", [])), "experiment_id": record.get("experiment_id")})
    88 |     return rows
    89 | 
    90 | 
    91 | def load_training_rows(dataset_path: str | Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    92 |     recorder = GroundTruthRecorder(dataset_path)
    93 |     return flatten_records(recorder.read())

1 | """Controlled PostgreSQL fault injection for the Database Fault Laboratory.
     2 | 
     3 | These actions are intentionally explicit and are only suitable for an
     4 | isolated lab database.  The monitored-database tools remain read-only.
     5 | """
     6 | 
     7 | from __future__ import annotations
     8 | 
     9 | from collections.abc import Mapping
    10 | from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    11 | from enum import StrEnum
    12 | from typing import Any, Awaitable, Callable
    13 | 
    14 | 
    15 | class FaultType(StrEnum):
    16 |     STALE_STATISTICS = "STALE_STATISTICS"
    17 |     PLAN_FLIP = "PLAN_FLIP"
    18 |     CARDINALITY_MISESTIMATION = "CARDINALITY_MISESTIMATION"
    19 |     LOCK_CONTENTION = "LOCK_CONTENTION"
    20 |     VACUUM_LAG = "VACUUM_LAG"
    21 |     INDEX_MISSING = "INDEX_MISSING"
    22 |     INDEX_UNUSED = "INDEX_UNUSED"
    23 |     IO_SATURATION = "IO_SATURATION"
    24 |     BUFFER_PRESSURE = "BUFFER_PRESSURE"
    25 | 
    26 | 
    27 | @dataclass(frozen=True)
    28 | class FaultScenario:
    29 |     """A reproducible fault definition and its classifier labels."""
    30 | 
    31 |     name: str
    32 |     labels: tuple[str, ...]
    33 |     parameters: Mapping[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    34 | 
    35 | 
    36 | FAULT_MATRIX: dict[str, FaultScenario] = {
    37 |     fault.value: FaultScenario(fault.value.lower(), (fault.value,))
    38 |     for fault in FaultType
    39 | }
    40 | 
    41 | 
    42 | def scenario(name: str, **parameters: Any) -> FaultScenario:
    43 |     """Return a named matrix scenario with parameter overrides."""
    44 |     try:
    45 |         base = FAULT_MATRIX[name.upper()]
    46 |     except KeyError as exc:
    47 |         raise ValueError(f"Unknown fault scenario: {name}") from exc
    48 |     return FaultScenario(base.name, base.labels, {**base.parameters, **parameters})
    49 | 
    50 | 
    51 | async def apply_fault(connection: Any, fault: FaultScenario) -> dict[str, Any]:
    52 |     """Apply one fault to an asyncpg-compatible lab connection.
    53 | 
    54 |     The caller owns the lab schema and transaction.  Statements use fixed
    55 |     identifiers; configurable values are passed as bound parameters where
    56 |     PostgreSQL permits them.
    57 |     """
    58 |     table = str(fault.parameters.get("table", "fault_lab_orders"))
    59 |     if not table.replace("_", "").isalnum() or not table[0].isalpha():
    60 |         raise ValueError("Invalid lab table identifier")
    61 |     statements: list[str] = []
    62 |     if FaultType.STALE_STATISTICS.value in fault.labels:
    63 |         statements.append(f"INSERT INTO {table} (customer_id, amount) SELECT 999999, 1 FROM generate_series(1, 1000)")
    64 |         statements.append("ALTER TABLE " + table + " ALTER COLUMN customer_id SET STATISTICS 1")
    65 |     elif FaultType.PLAN_FLIP.value in fault.labels:
    66 |         statements.append(f"INSERT INTO {table} (customer_id, amount) SELECT 1000000 + g, g FROM generate_series(1, 5000) AS g")
    67 |     elif FaultType.CARDINALITY_MISESTIMATION.value in fault.labels:
    68 |         statements.append(f"INSERT INTO {table} (customer_id, amount) SELECT 7, g FROM generate_series(1, 10000) AS g")
    69 |     elif FaultType.VACUUM_LAG.value in fault.labels:
    70 |         statements.append(f"UPDATE {table} SET amount = amount + 1 WHERE id % 2 = 0")
    71 |     elif FaultType.INDEX_MISSING.value in fault.labels:
    72 |         statements.append(f"DROP INDEX IF EXISTS {table}_customer_id_idx")
    73 |     elif FaultType.INDEX_UNUSED.value in fault.labels:
    74 |         statements.append(f"CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS {table}_customer_id_idx ON {table} (customer_id)")
    75 |     elif FaultType.IO_SATURATION.value in fault.labels or FaultType.BUFFER_PRESSURE.value in fault.labels:
    76 |         statements.append(f"SELECT a.id, b.id FROM {table} a CROSS JOIN {table} b LIMIT 10000")
    77 |     elif FaultType.LOCK_CONTENTION.value in fault.labels:
    78 |         # The held transaction must remain open; use hold_lock() for that case.
    79 |         statements.append(f"SELECT id FROM {table} WHERE id = 1 FOR UPDATE")
    80 | 
    81 |     for statement in statements:
    82 |         await connection.execute(statement)
    83 |     return {"scenario": fault.name, "labels": list(fault.labels), "statements": statements}
    84 | 
    85 | 
    86 | async def hold_lock(connection: Any, table: str = "fault_lab_orders", row_id: int = 1) -> None:
    87 |     """Acquire a lock and keep the caller's transaction open for contention."""
    88 |     if not table.replace("_", "").isalnum() or not table[0].isalpha():
    89 |         raise ValueError("Invalid lab table identifier")
    90 |     await connection.execute(f"SELECT id FROM {table} WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE", row_id)
    91 | 
    92 | 
    93 | async def run_scenario(
    94 |     connection: Any,
    95 |     fault: FaultScenario,
    96 |     telemetry_reader: Callable[[Any], Awaitable[list[Mapping[str, Any]]]],
    97 |     recorder: Any,
    98 |     *,
    99 |     workload: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
   100 | ) -> Any:
   101 |     """Apply, observe, and persist one labeled fault-lab experiment."""
   102 |     await apply_fault(connection, fault)
   103 |     telemetry = await telemetry_reader(connection)
   104 |     return recorder.record(
   105 |         scenario=fault.name,
   106 |         labels=fault.labels,
   107 |         telemetry=telemetry,
   108 |         workload=workload,
   109 |         fault_parameters=fault.parameters,
   110 |     )

1 | """pgbench workload generation for the fault laboratory."""
     2 | 
     3 | from __future__ import annotations
     4 | 
     5 | import asyncio
     6 | import shlex
     7 | from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     8 | from typing import Sequence
     9 | 
    10 | 
    11 | @dataclass(frozen=True)
    12 | class WorkloadConfig:
    13 |     dsn: str
    14 |     clients: int = 4
    15 |     threads: int = 2
    16 |     duration_seconds: int = 30
    17 |     scale: int = 10
    18 |     extra_args: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)
    19 | 
    20 | 
    21 | def pgbench_command(config: WorkloadConfig) -> list[str]:
    22 |     """Build a safe pgbench command without shell interpolation."""
    23 |     if config.clients < 1 or config.threads < 1 or config.duration_seconds < 1:
    24 |         raise ValueError("clients, threads, and duration_seconds must be positive")
    25 |     return [
    26 |         "pgbench",
    27 |         "-c", str(config.clients),
    28 |         "-j", str(config.threads),
    29 |         "-T", str(config.duration_seconds),
    30 |         *config.extra_args,
    31 |         config.dsn,
    32 |     ]
    33 | 
    34 | 
    35 | async def run_pgbench(config: WorkloadConfig) -> dict[str, object]:
    36 |     """Run pgbench and return reproducibility metadata and captured output."""
    37 |     command = pgbench_command(config)
    38 |     process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
    39 |         *command,
    40 |         stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    41 |         stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    42 |     )
    43 |     stdout, stderr = await process.communicate()
    44 |     return {
    45 |         "command": shlex.join(command),
    46 |         "returncode": process.returncode,
    47 |         "stdout": stdout.decode(errors="replace"),
    48 |         "stderr": stderr.decode(errors="replace"),
    49 |         "success": process.returncode == 0,
    50 |     }
    51 | 
    52 | 
    53 | async def run_sql_workload(connection: object, statements: Sequence[str]) -> int:
    54 |     """Execute fixed lab statements when pgbench is unavailable in CI."""
    55 |     for statement in statements:
    56 |         await connection.execute(statement)
    57 |     return len(statements)

1 | """Feature and label contracts for the root-cause classifier."""
     2 | 
     3 | from __future__ import annotations
     4 | 
     5 | from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
     6 | from typing import Any
     7 | 
     8 | import numpy as np
     9 | 
    10 | 
    11 | CAUSES = (
    12 |     "STALE_STATISTICS",
    13 |     "PLAN_FLIP",
    14 |     "CARDINALITY_MISESTIMATION",
    15 |     "LOCK_CONTENTION",
    16 |     "INDEX_MISSING",
    17 |     "INDEX_UNUSED",
    18 |     "VACUUM_LAG",
    19 |     "BLOAT",
    20 |     "BUFFER_PRESSURE",
    21 |     "IO_SATURATION",
    22 |     "TEMP_SPILL",
    23 |     "CONNECTION_CONTENTION",
    24 |     "CHECKPOINT_PRESSURE",
    25 |     "UNKNOWN",
    26 | )
    27 | 
    28 | FEATURE_NAMES = (
    29 |     "cardinality_error",
    30 |     "plan_flip",
    31 |     "estimated_cost",
    32 |     "actual_time",
    33 |     "buffer_hit_ratio",
    34 |     "buffer_reads",
    35 |     "lock_wait_seconds",
    36 |     "dead_tuple_ratio",
    37 |     "vacuum_age",
    38 |     "analyze_age",
    39 |     "table_growth_rate",
    40 |     "idx_scan_ratio",
    41 |     "temp_io",
    42 |     "wal_rate",
    43 |     "connection_count",
    44 |     "latency_p95",
    45 | )
    46 | 
    47 | 
    48 | def _number(row: Mapping[str, Any], *names: str) -> float:
    49 |     for name in names:
    50 |         value = row.get(name)
    51 |         if value is not None:
    52 |             return float(value)
    53 |     return 0.0
    54 | 
    55 | 
    56 | def extract_features(row: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, float]:
    57 |     hits = _number(row, "buffer_hits", "shared_blks_hit")
    58 |     reads = _number(row, "buffer_reads", "shared_blks_read")
    59 |     scans = _number(row, "idx_scans", "idx_scan")
    60 |     seq_scans = _number(row, "seq_scans", "seq_scan")
    61 |     return {
    62 |         "cardinality_error": _number(row, "cardinality_error"),
    63 |         "plan_flip": _number(row, "plan_flip", "plan_changed"),
    64 |         "estimated_cost": _number(row, "estimated_cost"),
    65 |         "actual_time": _number(row, "actual_time", "execution_time", "mean_exec_time"),
    66 |         "buffer_hit_ratio": _number(row, "buffer_hit_ratio") or hits / max(hits + reads, 1.0),
    67 |         "buffer_reads": reads,
    68 |         "lock_wait_seconds": _number(row, "lock_wait_seconds", "lock_wait"),
    69 |         "dead_tuple_ratio": _number(row, "dead_tuple_ratio"),
    70 |         "vacuum_age": _number(row, "vacuum_age"),
    71 |         "analyze_age": _number(row, "analyze_age"),
    72 |         "table_growth_rate": _number(row, "table_growth_rate", "table_size_bytes_growth_rate"),
    73 |         "idx_scan_ratio": _number(row, "idx_scan_ratio") or scans / max(scans + seq_scans, 1.0),
    74 |         "temp_io": _number(row, "temp_io") + _number(row, "temp_blks_read", "temp_blks_written"),
    75 |         "wal_rate": _number(row, "wal_rate", "wal_bytes"),
    76 |         "connection_count": _number(row, "connection_count", "connections"),
    77 |         "latency_p95": _number(row, "latency_p95", "p95_latency", "max_exec_time"),
    78 |     }
    79 | 
    80 | 
    81 | def build_feature_matrix(rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> np.ndarray:
    82 |     return np.asarray(
    83 |         [[extract_features(row)[name] for name in FEATURE_NAMES] for row in rows],
    84 |         dtype=np.float32,
    85 |     )
    86 | 
    87 | 
    88 | def build_label_matrix(rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> np.ndarray:
    89 |     matrix = np.zeros((len(rows), len(CAUSES)), dtype=np.int32)
    90 |     for row_index, row in enumerate(rows):
    91 |         labels = row.get("labels", row.get("causes", []))
    92 |         if isinstance(labels, str):
    93 |             labels = [labels]
    94 |         for label in labels:
    95 |             if label in CAUSES:
    96 |                 matrix[row_index, CAUSES.index(label)] = 1
    97 |     return matrix

1 | """Inference and deterministic causal ranking for root-cause predictions."""
     2 | 
     3 | from __future__ import annotations
     4 | 
     5 | import os
     6 | from collections.abc import Mapping
     7 | from pathlib import Path
     8 | from typing import Any
     9 | 
    10 | import joblib
    11 | import numpy as np
    12 | 
    13 | from app.ml.rca_classifier.features import CAUSES, build_feature_matrix
    14 | 
    15 | 
    16 | def _load(path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    17 |     return joblib.load(Path(path or os.getenv("RCA_MODEL_PATH", "rca_model.joblib")))
    18 | 
    19 | 
    20 | def rank_causes(
    21 |     probabilities: Mapping[str, float],
    22 |     evidence_strength: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    23 | ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    24 |     """Rank causes without changing model probabilities or inventing evidence."""
    25 |     evidence_strength = evidence_strength or {}
    26 |     ranked = []
    27 |     for cause, probability in probabilities.items():
    28 |         score = float(np.clip(probability, 0.0, 1.0))
    29 |         if evidence_strength.get(cause) is not None:
    30 |             score *= float(np.clip(evidence_strength[cause], 0.0, 1.0))
    31 |         rank = "PRIMARY" if score >= 0.65 else "CONTRIBUTING" if score >= 0.35 else "CORRELATED" if score >= 0.15 else "UNRELATED"
    32 |         ranked.append({"cause": cause, "probability": float(np.clip(probability, 0.0, 1.0)), "score": score, "rank": rank})
    33 |     return sorted(ranked, key=lambda item: item["score"], reverse=True)
    34 | 
    35 | 
    36 | def predict(
    37 |     features: Mapping[str, Any],
    38 |     model_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    39 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    40 |     artifact = _load(model_path)
    41 |     values = build_feature_matrix([features])
    42 |     model = artifact["model"]
    43 |     raw = model.predict_proba(values)
    44 |     # OneVsRest returns either an ndarray or a list for edge-case estimators.
    45 |     probabilities = np.asarray(raw, dtype=object)
    46 |     if probabilities.ndim == 2:
    47 |         probabilities = probabilities[0]
    48 |     probabilities = [float(value[1] if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, np.ndarray)) and len(value) > 1 else value) for value in probabilities]
    49 |     probability_map = dict(zip(artifact.get("causes", CAUSES), np.clip(probabilities, 0.0, 1.0)))
    50 |     ranked = rank_causes(probability_map)
    51 |     return {"probabilities": probability_map, "ranked_causes": ranked}

1 | """Train the multi-label LightGBM root-cause classifier."""
     2 | 
     3 | from __future__ import annotations
     4 | 
     5 | import os
     6 | from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
     7 | from pathlib import Path
     8 | from typing import Any
     9 | 
    10 | import joblib
    11 | import numpy as np
    12 | from lightgbm import LGBMClassifier
    13 | from app.ml.rca_classifier.features import CAUSES, FEATURE_NAMES, build_feature_matrix, build_label_matrix
    14 | 
    15 | 
    16 | class MultiLabelLightGBM:
    17 |     """One binary LightGBM model per cause, with constant-label fallbacks."""
    18 | 
    19 |     def __init__(self, random_state: int = 42) -> None:
    20 |         self.random_state = random_state
    21 |         self.models: list[LGBMClassifier | None] = []
    22 |         self.constants: list[float | None] = []
    23 | 
    24 |     def fit(self, values: np.ndarray, labels: np.ndarray) -> "MultiLabelLightGBM":
    25 |         for column in range(labels.shape[1]):
    26 |             target = labels[:, column]
    27 |             unique = np.unique(target)
    28 |             if len(unique) < 2:
    29 |                 self.models.append(None)
    30 |                 self.constants.append(float(unique[0]))
    31 |                 continue
    32 |             model = LGBMClassifier(
    33 |                 n_estimators=80,
    34 |                 learning_rate=0.05,
    35 |                 num_leaves=15,
    36 |                 max_depth=4,
    37 |                 verbosity=-1,
    38 |                 random_state=self.random_state,
    39 |             ).fit(values, target)
    40 |             self.models.append(model)
    41 |             self.constants.append(None)
    42 |         return self
    43 | 
    44 |     def predict_proba(self, values: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    45 |         columns = []
    46 |         for model, constant in zip(self.models, self.constants):
    47 |             if model is None:
    48 |                 columns.append(np.full(len(values), constant, dtype=float))
    49 |             else:
    50 |                 columns.append(model.predict_proba(values)[:, 1])
    51 |         return np.column_stack(columns)
    52 | 
    53 | 
    54 | def train(
    55 |     rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    56 |     artifact_path: str | os.PathLike[str] = "rca_model.joblib",
    57 |     *,
    58 |     random_state: int = 42,
    59 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    60 |     values = build_feature_matrix(rows)
    61 |     labels = build_label_matrix(rows)
    62 |     if len(values) < 2:
    63 |         raise ValueError("At least two labeled telemetry rows are required")
    64 |     if not labels.any(axis=0).any():
    65 |         raise ValueError("Training rows must contain at least one recognized cause label")
    66 |     model = MultiLabelLightGBM(random_state).fit(values, labels)
    67 |     artifact = {"model": model, "feature_names": FEATURE_NAMES, "causes": CAUSES}
    68 |     path = Path(artifact_path)
    69 |     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    70 |     joblib.dump(artifact, path)
    71 |     _log_mlflow(path, len(values))
    72 |     return {"artifact_path": str(path), "rows": len(values), "causes": list(CAUSES)}
    73 | 
    74 | 
    75 | def _log_mlflow(path: Path, row_count: int) -> None:
    76 |     try:
    77 |         import mlflow
    78 | 
    79 |         mlflow.set_tracking_uri(os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI", "http://localhost:5000"))
    80 |         with mlflow.start_run(run_name="rca-lightgbm-multilabel"):
    81 |             mlflow.log_param("rows", row_count)
    82 |             mlflow.log_artifact(str(path), artifact_path="model")
    83 |     except Exception:
    84 |         return

1 | """Window construction for temporal anomaly detection."""
     2 | 
     3 | from __future__ import annotations
     4 | 
     5 | from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
     6 | from typing import Any
     7 | 
     8 | import numpy as np
     9 | 
    10 | from app.ml.anomaly.features import FEATURE_NAMES, extract_features
    11 | 
    12 | 
    13 | def row_features(row: Mapping[str, Any]) -> np.ndarray:
    14 |     return np.asarray([extract_features(row)[name] for name in FEATURE_NAMES], dtype=np.float32)
    15 | 
    16 | 
    17 | def build_windows(
    18 |     rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    19 |     window_size: int = 30,
    20 |     stride: int = 1,
    21 | ) -> np.ndarray:
    22 |     """Create chronological, overlapping windows of telemetry feature vectors."""
    23 |     if window_size < 2 or stride < 1:
    24 |         raise ValueError("window_size must be >= 2 and stride must be >= 1")
    25 |     values = np.asarray([row_features(row) for row in rows], dtype=np.float32)
    26 |     if len(values) < window_size:
    27 |         return np.empty((0, window_size, len(FEATURE_NAMES)), dtype=np.float32)
    28 |     return np.stack(
    29 |         [values[start : start + window_size] for start in range(0, len(values) - window_size + 1, stride)]
    30 |     )

    17 | def _load(path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    18 |     return torch.load(path or os.getenv("TEMPORAL_MODEL_PATH", "temporal_model.pt"), map_location="cpu")
    19 | 
    20 | 
    21 | def predict(
    22 |     window: Sequence[Sequence[float]] | np.ndarray,
    23 |     model_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    24 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    25 |     artifact = _load(model_path)
    26 |     values = torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(window, dtype=np.float32)).unsqueeze(0)
    27 |     if values.shape[1] != artifact["timesteps"] or values.shape[2] != artifact["input_size"]:
    28 |         raise ValueError("window shape does not match the trained temporal model")
    29 |     model = LSTMAutoencoder(artifact["input_size"], artifact["hidden_size"], artifact["latent_size"])
    30 |     model.load_state_dict(artifact["state_dict"])
    31 |     model.eval()
    32 |     with torch.no_grad():
    33 |         reconstruction_error = float(((model(values) - values) ** 2).mean().item())
    34 |     threshold = float(artifact["threshold"])
    35 |     probability = 1.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(-8.0 * (reconstruction_error / max(threshold, 1e-8) - 1.0)))
    36 |     return {
    37 |         "anomaly_probability": float(np.clip(probability, 0.0, 1.0)),
    38 |         "reconstruction_error": reconstruction_error,
    39 |         "threshold": threshold,
    40 |         "is_anomaly": reconstruction_error > threshold,
    41 |     }

chunk_a4ca77f9de6de5c3.numbered_code:
1 | """Train a PyTorch LSTM autoencoder over telemetry windows."""
     2 | 
     3 | from __future__ import annotations
     4 | 
     5 | import os
     6 | from collections.abc import Sequence
     7 | from pathlib import Path
     8 | from typing import Any
     9 | 
    10 | import numpy as np
    11 | import torch
    12 | from torch import nn
    13 | 
    14 | from app.ml.temporal.features import build_windows
    15 | 
    16 | 
    17 | class LSTMAutoencoder(nn.Module):
    18 |     def __init__(self, input_size: int, hidden_size: int = 32, latent_size: int = 16) -> None:
    19 |         super().__init__()
    20 |         self.encoder = nn.LSTM(input_size, hidden_size, batch_first=True)
    21 |         self.to_latent = nn.Linear(hidden_size, latent_size)
    22 |         self.from_latent = nn.Linear(latent_size, hidden_size)
    23 |         self.decoder = nn.LSTM(hidden_size, hidden_size, batch_first=True)
    24 |         self.output = nn.Linear(hidden_size, input_size)
    25 | 
    26 |     def forward(self, values: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    27 |         encoded, _ = self.encoder(values)
    28 |         latent = self.to_latent(encoded[:, -1])
    29 |         repeated = self.from_latent(latent).unsqueeze(1).repeat(1, values.size(1), 1)
    30 |         decoded, _ = self.decoder(repeated)
    31 |         return self.output(decoded)
    32 | 
    33 | 
    34 | def train(
    35 |     windows: np.ndarray | Sequence[Sequence[Sequence[float]]],
    36 |     artifact_path: str | os.PathLike[str] = "temporal_model.pt",
    37 |     *,
    38 |     epochs: int = 10,
    39 |     hidden_size: int = 32,
    40 |     latent_size: int = 16,
    41 |     learning_rate: float = 1e-3,
    42 |     random_seed: int = 42,
    43 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    44 |     """Train on windows shaped ``(samples, timesteps, features)``."""
    45 |     torch.manual_seed(random_seed)
    46 |     values = torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(windows, dtype=np.float32))
    47 |     if values.ndim != 3 or values.shape[0] < 2:
    48 |         raise ValueError("At least two temporal windows are required")
    49 |     model = LSTMAutoencoder(values.shape[2], hidden_size, latent_size)
    50 |     optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
    51 |     loss_fn = nn.MSELoss()
    52 |     model.train()
    53 |     for _ in range(max(1, epochs)):
    54 |         optimizer.zero_grad()
    55 |         loss = loss_fn(model(values), values)
    56 |         loss.backward()
    57 |         optimizer.step()
    58 |     model.eval()
    59 |     with torch.no_grad():
    60 |         errors = ((model(values) - values) ** 2).mean(dim=(1, 2)).numpy()
    61 |     threshold = float(np.quantile(errors, 0.95))
    62 |     path = Path(artifact_path)
    63 |     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    64 |     torch.save(
    65 |         {
    66 |             "state_dict": model.state_dict(),
    67 |             "input_size": int(values.shape[2]),
    68 |             "timesteps": int(values.shape[1]),
    69 |             "hidden_size": hidden_size,
    70 |             "latent_size": latent_size,
    71 |             "threshold": threshold,
    72 |         },
    73 |         path,
    74 |     )
    75 |     _log_mlflow(path, len(values), epochs, threshold)
    76 |     return {"artifact_path": str(path), "windows": len(values), "threshold": threshold}
    77 | 
    78 | 
    79 | def train_from_rows(
    80 |     rows: Sequence[dict[str, Any]],
    81 |     artifact_path: str | os.PathLike[str] = "temporal_model.pt",
    82 |     *,
    83 |     window_size: int = 30,
    84 |     **kwargs: Any,
    85 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    86 |     return train(build_windows(rows, window_size=window_size), artifact_path, **kwargs)
    87 | 
    88 | 
    89 | def _log_mlflow(path: Path, window_count: int, epochs: int, threshold: float) -> None:
    90 |     try:
    91 |         import mlflow
    92 | 
    93 |         mlflow.set_tracking_uri(os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI", "http://localhost:5000"))
    94 |         with mlflow.start_run(run_name="temporal-lstm-autoencoder"):
    95 |             mlflow.log_params({"windows": window_count, "epochs": epochs})
    96 |             mlflow.log_metric("reconstruction_threshold", threshold)
    97 |             mlflow.log_artifact(str(path), artifact_path="model")
    98 |     except Exception:
    99 |         return

    40 | 
    41 | async def _snapshot(connection: asyncpg.Connection, table: str, query: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    42 |     captured_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    43 |     plan = await pg_introspection.get_explain_plan(connection, query)
    44 |     query_rows = await pg_introspection.get_query_metrics(connection, limit=25)
    45 |     query_row = max(query_rows, key=lambda row: float(row.get("total_exec_time") or 0), default={})
    46 |     table_rows = await pg_introspection.get_table_stats(connection, table=table)
    47 |     table_row = table_rows[0] if table_rows else {}
    48 |     buffer_rows = await pg_introspection.get_buffer_stats(connection)
    49 |     buffer_row = next((row for row in buffer_rows if row.get("relname") == table), {})
    50 |     activity = await pg_introspection.get_pg_activity(connection)
    51 |     locks = await pg_introspection.get_pg_locks(connection)
    52 |     waiting = [
    53 |         row for row in activity
    54 |         if str(row.get("wait_event_type") or "").lower() == "lock"
    55 |         or row.get("pid") in {lock.get("pid") for lock in locks if lock.get("granted") is False}
    56 |     ]
    57 |     live = float(table_row.get("n_live_tup") or 0)
    58 |     dead = float(table_row.get("n_dead_tup") or 0)
    59 |     seq_scans = float(table_row.get("seq_scan") or 0)
    60 |     idx_scans = float(table_row.get("idx_scan") or 0)
    61 |     heap_reads = float(buffer_row.get("heap_blks_read") or 0)
    62 |     heap_hits = float(buffer_row.get("heap_blks_hit") or 0)
    63 |     analyze_at = table_row.get("last_analyze") or table_row.get("last_autoanalyze")
    64 |     vacuum_at = table_row.get("last_vacuum") or table_row.get("last_autovacuum")
    65 |     analyze_age = max(0.0, (captured_at - analyze_at).total_seconds() / 3600) if analyze_at else 0.0
    66 |     vacuum_age = max(0.0, (captured_at - vacuum_at).total_seconds() / 3600) if vacuum_at else 0.0
    67 |     estimated_rows = float(plan.get("estimated_rows") or 0)
    68 |     actual_rows = float(plan.get("actual_rows") or 0)
    69 |     return {
    70 |         "timestamp": captured_at.isoformat(),
    71 |         "query_hash": plan.get("query_hash"),
    72 |         "table_name": table,
    73 |         "estimated_rows": estimated_rows,
    74 |         "actual_rows": actual_rows,
    75 |         "estimated_cost": plan.get("estimated_cost"),
    76 |         "actual_time": plan.get("actual_time"),
    77 |         "execution_time": float(query_row.get("total_exec_time") or plan.get("actual_time") or 0),
    78 |         "latency_p50": float(query_row.get("mean_exec_time") or plan.get("actual_time") or 0),
    79 |         "latency_p95": float(query_row.get("max_exec_time") or plan.get("actual_time") or 0),
    80 |         "planning_time": float(query_row.get("planning_time") or 0),
    81 |         "buffer_hits": plan.get("buffer_hits", heap_hits),
    82 |         "buffer_reads": plan.get("buffer_reads", heap_reads),
    83 |         "buffer_hit_ratio": heap_hits / max(heap_hits + heap_reads, 1.0),
    84 |         "dead_tuple_ratio": dead / max(live + dead, 1.0),
    85 |         "idx_scan_ratio": idx_scans / max(idx_scans + seq_scans, 1.0),
    86 |         "lock_wait_seconds": float(len(waiting)),
    87 |         "connection_count": len(activity),
    88 |         "temp_io": 0.0,
    89 |         "temp_blks_read": float(query_row.get("temp_blks_read") or 0),
    90 |         "temp_blks_written": float(query_row.get("temp_blks_written") or 0),
    91 |         "wal_rate": float(query_row.get("wal_bytes") or 0),
    92 |         "plan_flip": 0.0,
    93 |         "table_growth_rate": 0.0,
    94 |         "analyze_age": analyze_age,
    95 |         "vacuum_age": vacuum_age,
    96 |         "cardinality_error": math.log1p(actual_rows) - math.log1p(estimated_rows),
    97 |     }

1 | """Train the anomaly detector from application-database telemetry.

     4 | RCA classifier and temporal/outcome models have separate laboratory datasets
     5 | and must not be trained from unlabeled production snapshots.

    11 | import asyncio
    12 | from pathlib import Path
    13 |

    17 | from app.db.session import async_session_factory

    22 | def _row(metric: QueryMetric) -> dict[str, float]:
    23 |     return {
    24 |         "timestamp": metric.timestamp.isoformat(),
    25 |         "calls": metric.calls,
    26 |         "execution_time": metric.mean_exec_time,
    27 |         "latency_p50": metric.mean_exec_time,

    45 |         if limit:
