chunk_24f6caa9224e4c4a.numbered_code:
1 | """Audit Logging & Observability Service.
     2 | 
     3 | Provides centralized helpers for recording immutable audit trail logs and
     4 | querying system audit records per PRD.md §14, §15, §22.
     5 | """
     6 | 
     7 | from __future__ import annotations
     8 | 
     9 | import uuid
    10 | from datetime import datetime, timezone
    11 | from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
    12 | from sqlalchemy import select, func
    13 | from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
    14 | 
    15 | from app.core.logging import get_logger
    16 | from app.models.audit import AuditLog, CanaryRun
    17 | from app.schemas.audit import AuditLogListResponse, AuditLogOut
    18 | 
    19 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
    20 | 
    21 | 
    22 | class AuditService:
    23 |     """Service managing audit trail records and query logging."""
    24 | 
    25 |     async def log_event(
    26 |         self,
    27 |         db: AsyncSession,
    28 |         action_type: str,
    29 |         target_entity: str,
    30 |         target_id: Optional[str] = None,
    31 |         user_id: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None,
    32 |         connection_id: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None,
    33 |         details: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    34 |         ip_address: Optional[str] = None,
    35 |     ) -> AuditLog:
    36 |         """Create and persist an immutable audit trail entry."""
    37 |         now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    38 |         entry = AuditLog(
    39 |             user_id=user_id,
    40 |             connection_id=connection_id,
    41 |             action_type=action_type,
    42 |             target_entity=target_entity,
    43 |             target_id=target_id,
    44 |             details=details or {},
    45 |             ip_address=ip_address,
    46 |             timestamp=now,
    47 |         )
    48 |         db.add(entry)
    49 |         await db.commit()
    50 |         await db.refresh(entry)
    51 | 
    52 |         logger.info(
    53 |             f"Audit log created: action='{action_type}', entity='{target_entity}'",
    54 |             extra={
    55 |                 "action": action_type,
    56 |                 "target_entity": target_entity,
    57 |                 "target_id": target_id,
    58 |                 "connection_id": str(connection_id) if connection_id else None,
    59 |                 "user_id": str(user_id) if user_id else None,
    60 |             },
    61 |         )
    62 |         return entry
    63 | 
    64 |     async def list_audit_logs(
    65 |         self,
    66 |         db: AsyncSession,
    67 |         connection_id: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None,
    68 |         user_id: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None,
    69 |         action_type: Optional[str] = None,
    70 |         target_entity: Optional[str] = None,
    71 |         limit: int = 50,
    72 |         offset: int = 0,
    73 |     ) -> AuditLogListResponse:
    74 |         """Query and paginate audit logs with optional filters."""
    75 |         stmt = select(AuditLog)
    76 |         count_stmt = select(func.count(AuditLog.id))
    77 | 
    78 |         if connection_id is not None:
    79 |             stmt = stmt.where(AuditLog.connection_id == connection_id)
    80 |             count_stmt = count_stmt.where(AuditLog.connection_id == connection_id)
    81 |         if user_id is not None:
    82 |             stmt = stmt.where(AuditLog.user_id == user_id)
    83 |             count_stmt = count_stmt.where(AuditLog.user_id == user_id)
    84 |         if action_type is not None:
    85 |             stmt = stmt.where(AuditLog.action_type == action_type)
    86 |             count_stmt = count_stmt.where(AuditLog.action_type == action_type)
    87 |         if target_entity is not None:
    88 |             stmt = stmt.where(AuditLog.target_entity == target_entity)
    89 |             count_stmt = count_stmt.where(AuditLog.target_entity == target_entity)
    90 | 
    91 |         total = await db.scalar(count_stmt) or 0
    92 | 
    93 |         stmt = stmt.order_by(AuditLog.timestamp.desc()).offset(offset).limit(limit)
    94 |         res = await db.execute(stmt)
    95 |         items = list(res.scalars().all())
    96 | 
    97 |         return AuditLogListResponse(
    98 |             total=total,
    99 |             items=[AuditLogOut.model_validate(item) for item in items],
   100 |         )
   101 | 
   102 |     async def list_canary_runs(
   103 |         self,
   104 |         db: AsyncSession,
   105 |         connection_id: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None,
   106 |         experiment_id: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None,
   107 |         limit: int = 20,
   108 |     ) -> List[CanaryRun]:
   109 |         """Query canary deployment history."""
   110 |         stmt = select(CanaryRun)
   111 |         if connection_id is not None:
   112 |             stmt = stmt.where(CanaryRun.connection_id == connection_id)
   113 |         if experiment_id is not None:
   114 |             stmt = stmt.where(CanaryRun.experiment_id == experiment_id)
   115 |         stmt = stmt.order_by(CanaryRun.started_at.desc()).limit(limit)
   116 |         res = await db.execute(stmt)
   117 |         return list(res.scalars().all())
   118 | 
   119 | 
   120 | audit_service = AuditService()

    37 | async def _provision_monitoring_dsn(raw_conn_str: str, *, rotate_existing: bool = True) -> tuple[str, str]:
    38 |     """Create a dedicated read-only role and return a DSN for that role."""
    39 |     owner_dsn = _prepare_asyncpg_dsn(raw_conn_str)
    40 |     parsed = urlsplit(owner_dsn)
    41 |     if not parsed.hostname or not parsed.path.strip("/"):
    42 |         raise ValueError("A URL connection string is required to provision a monitoring role")
    43 | 
    44 |     target_key = f"{parsed.hostname}:{parsed.port or 5432}/{parsed.path.strip('/')}"
    45 |     role_name = f"zentrix_monitor_{hashlib.sha256(target_key.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]}"
    46 |     role_password = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    47 |     role_identifier = _quote_identifier(role_name)
    48 | 
    49 |     owner = await asyncpg.connect(owner_dsn, timeout=15.0)
    50 |     try:
    51 |         # The owner credential is used only for setup; it is never stored as the
    52 |         # monitoring credential after this function succeeds.
    53 |         await owner.execute("CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements")
    54 |         role_exists = await owner.fetchval(
    55 |             "SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = $1",
    56 |             role_name,
    57 |         )
    58 |         if role_exists and not rotate_existing:
    59 |             raise ValueError(
    60 |                 "The dedicated monitoring role already exists. Register the connection to rotate and save its credentials."
    61 |             )
    62 |         await owner.execute(
    63 |             "SELECT set_config('zentrix.monitoring_password', $1, false)",
    64 |             role_password,
    65 |         )
    66 |         if role_exists:
    67 |             await owner.execute(
    68 |                 """
    69 |                 DO $zentrix$
    70 |                 BEGIN
    71 |                     EXECUTE format(
    72 |                         'ALTER ROLE %I LOGIN PASSWORD %L',
    73 |                         $role_name$ROLE_NAME$role_name$,
    74 |                         current_setting('zentrix.monitoring_password')
    75 |                     );
    76 |                 END
    77 |                 $zentrix$
    78 |                 """.replace("ROLE_NAME", role_name)
    79 |             )
    80 |         else:
    81 |             await owner.execute(
    82 |                 """
    83 |                 DO $zentrix$
    84 |                 BEGIN
    85 |                     EXECUTE format(
    86 |                         'CREATE ROLE %I LOGIN PASSWORD %L',
    87 |                         $role_name$ROLE_NAME$role_name$,
    88 |                         current_setting('zentrix.monitoring_password')
    89 |                     );
    90 |                 END
    91 |                 $zentrix$
    92 |                 """.replace("ROLE_NAME", role_name)
    93 |             )
    94 | 
    95 |         database_name = await owner.fetchval("SELECT current_database()")
    96 |         database_identifier = _quote_identifier(str(database_name))
    97 |         await owner.execute(f"GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE {database_identifier} TO {role_identifier}")
    98 |         await owner.execute(f"GRANT pg_monitor TO {role_identifier}")
    99 |         await owner.execute(f"GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO {role_identifier}")
   100 |         await owner.execute(f"GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO {role_identifier}")
   101 |         await owner.execute(
   102 |             f"ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO {role_identifier}"
   103 |         )
   104 |         await owner.execute(f"REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM {role_identifier}")
   105 |         # Clear setup statements while the owner/admin connection still has
   106 |         # permission to reset the target's query-stat history.
   107 |         await owner.fetchval("SELECT pg_stat_statements_reset()")
   108 |     finally:
   109 |         await owner.close()

   120 | async def verify_raw_dsn(raw_conn_str: str) -> ConnectionTestResponse:
   121 |     """
   122 |     Connect to a PostgreSQL target using asyncpg, test credentials, measure latency,
   123 |     and verify required extensions and view permissions.
   124 |     """
   125 | 
   126 |     dsn = _prepare_asyncpg_dsn(raw_conn_str)
   127 |     permissions: Dict[str, bool] = {
   128 |         "pg_stat_statements": False,
   129 |         "hypopg": False,
   130 |         "pg_stat_activity": False,
   131 |         "pg_stat_user_tables": False,
   132 |         "pg_statio_user_tables": False,
   133 |         "read_only_role": False,
   134 |     }
   135 |     postgres_version: Optional[str] = None
   136 |     start_time = time.perf_counter()
   137 | 
   138 |     try:
   139 |         conn = await asyncpg.connect(dsn, timeout=10.0)
   140 |     except Exception as e:
   141 |         logger.warning(f"Connection test failed: {e}")
   142 |         return ConnectionTestResponse(
   143 |             success=False,
   144 |             postgres_version=None,
   145 |             permissions=permissions,
   146 |             latency_ms=None,
   147 |             error=f"Connection failed: {str(e)}",
   148 |         )
   149 | 
   150 |     try:
   151 |         # 1. Measure latency with simple ping
   152 |         await conn.fetchval("SELECT 1;")
   153 |         latency_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000, 2)
   154 | 
   155 |         # 2. Get server version
   156 |         postgres_version = await conn.fetchval("SELECT version();")
   157 | 
   158 |         # 3. Check pg_stat_statements extension & query permission
   159 |         try:
   160 |             ext_exists = await conn.fetchval(
   161 |                 "SELECT 1 FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'pg_stat_statements';"
   162 |             )
   163 |             if ext_exists:
   164 |                 # Test querying the view
   165 |                 await conn.fetchval("SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_statements LIMIT 1;")
   166 |                 permissions["pg_stat_statements"] = True
   167 |         except Exception:
   168 |             permissions["pg_stat_statements"] = False
   169 | 
   170 |         # 4. Check hypopg extension (optional / recommended)
   171 |         try:
   172 |             hypopg_exists = await conn.fetchval(
   173 |                 "SELECT 1 FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'hypopg';"
   174 |             )
   175 |             if hypopg_exists:
   176 |                 permissions["hypopg"] = True
   177 |         except Exception:
   178 |             permissions["hypopg"] = False
   179 | 
   180 |         # 5. Check pg_stat_activity access
   181 |         try:
   182 |             await conn.fetchval("SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity LIMIT 1;")
   183 |             permissions["pg_stat_activity"] = True
   184 |         except Exception:
   185 |             permissions["pg_stat_activity"] = False
   186 | 
   187 |         # 6. Check pg_stat_user_tables access
   188 |         try:
   189 |             await conn.fetchval("SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_user_tables LIMIT 1;")
   190 |             permissions["pg_stat_user_tables"] = True
   191 |         except Exception:
   192 |             permissions["pg_stat_user_tables"] = False
   193 | 
   194 |         # 7. Check pg_statio_user_tables access
   195 |         try:
   196 |             await conn.fetchval("SELECT count(*) FROM pg_statio_user_tables LIMIT 1;")
   197 |             permissions["pg_statio_user_tables"] = True
   198 |         except Exception:
   199 |             permissions["pg_statio_user_tables"] = False
   200 | 
   201 |         # 8. Check that the monitoring role is not an elevated write-capable role.
   202 |         # Keep this as an explicit warning for now so existing targets can still
   203 |         # be inspected while the user creates a dedicated monitoring role.
   204 |         try:
   205 |             read_only = await conn.fetchval(
   206 |                 """
   207 |                 SELECT NOT rolsuper
   208 |                    AND NOT rolcreaterole
   209 |                    AND NOT rolcreatedb
   210 |                    AND NOT has_schema_privilege(current_user, 'public', 'CREATE')
   211 |                 FROM pg_roles
   212 |                 WHERE rolname = current_user;
   213 |                 """
   214 |             )
   215 |             permissions["read_only_role"] = bool(read_only)
   216 |         except Exception:
   217 |             permissions["read_only_role"] = False
   218 | 
   219 |         # Build response
   220 |         missing = []
   221 |         if not permissions["pg_stat_statements"]:
   222 |             missing.append("pg_stat_statements (required for query telemetry)")
   223 | 
   224 |         error_msg = None
   225 |         if missing:
   226 |             error_msg = f"Connected successfully, but required monitoring checks failed: {', '.join(missing)}"
   227 | 
   228 |         return ConnectionTestResponse(
   229 |             success=True,
   230 |             postgres_version=postgres_version,
   231 |             permissions=permissions,
   232 |             latency_ms=latency_ms,
   233 |             error=error_msg,
   234 |         )
   235 | 
   236 |     finally:
   237 |         await conn.close()

    57 | def _query_evidence(queries: list[QueryMetric], plans: list[PlanMetric], tables: list[TableMetric]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    58 |     plan_by_query: dict[uuid.UUID, list[PlanMetric]] = {}
    59 |     for plan in plans:
    60 |         if plan.query_metrics_id:
    61 |             plan_by_query.setdefault(plan.query_metrics_id, []).append(plan)
    62 | 
    63 |     query_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    64 |     for query in queries:
    65 |         row = _row(query)
    66 |         query_plans = sorted(plan_by_query.get(query.id, []), key=lambda item: item.timestamp)
    67 |         if query_plans:
    68 |             current = _row(query_plans[-1])
    69 |             row.update(current)
    70 |             row["cardinality_error"] = calculate_cardinality_error(current["estimated_rows"], current["actual_rows"])
    71 |             if len(query_plans) > 1:
    72 |                 row.update(diff_plans(_row(query_plans[-2]), current))
    73 |         row["latency_p95"] = query.max_exec_time
    74 |         row["temp_io"] = query.temp_blks_read + query.temp_blks_written
    75 |         row["wal_rate"] = query.wal_bytes
    76 |         query_rows.append(_json_safe(row))
    77 | 
    78 |     table_rows = []
    79 |     for table in tables:
    80 |         row = _row(table)
    81 |         row["idx_scan_ratio"] = table.idx_scans / max(table.idx_scans + table.seq_scans, 1)
    82 |         table_rows.append(_json_safe(row))
    83 | 
    84 |     # The graph expects one feature mapping. Preserve the strongest observed
    85 |     # signal for every feature so a vacuum signal is not hidden by query I/O.
    86 |     metrics: dict[str, Any] = {}
    87 |     for item in [*query_rows, *table_rows]:
    88 |         for key, value in item.items():
    89 |             if isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
    90 |                 metrics[key] = max(float(value), float(metrics.get(key, 0.0)))
    91 |             elif key not in metrics and value is not None:
    92 |                 metrics[key] = value
    93 |     timeline = [
    94 |         {"timestamp": item["timestamp"], "event": "query_telemetry", "query_hash": item.get("query_hash")}
    95 |         for item in query_rows
    96 |     ]
    97 |     return {
    98 |         "metrics": metrics,
    99 |         "query_metrics": query_rows,
   100 |         "table_metrics": table_rows,
   101 |         "plan_metrics": [_json_safe(_row(plan)) for plan in plans],
   102 |         "timeline": timeline,
   103 |     }

1 | """Deterministic computations over PostgreSQL telemetry.
     2 | 
     3 | This module deliberately has no database, model, or agent dependencies.  The
     4 | functions accept mappings so they can operate on rows returned by asyncpg as
     5 | well as normalized telemetry records loaded from the application database.
     6 | """
     7 | 
     8 | from __future__ import annotations
     9 | 
    10 | import math
    11 | from collections import defaultdict
    12 | from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
    13 | from datetime import datetime, timezone
    14 | from typing import Any
    15 | 
    16 | 
    17 | def _number(row: Mapping[str, Any], *names: str, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
    18 |     for name in names:
    19 |         value = row.get(name)
    20 |         if value is not None:
    21 |             return float(value)
    22 |     return default
    23 | 
    24 | 
    25 | def calculate_cardinality_error(
    26 |     estimated_rows: float | None, actual_rows: float | None
    27 | ) -> float:
    28 |     """Return signed log cardinality error, positive when estimates are low."""
    29 |     estimated = max(float(estimated_rows or 0), 0.0)
    30 |     actual = max(float(actual_rows or 0), 0.0)
    31 |     return math.log1p(actual) - math.log1p(estimated)
    32 | 
    33 | 
    34 | def diff_plans(previous: Mapping[str, Any], current: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    35 |     """Compare two executions of the same query and identify a plan flip."""
    36 |     previous_hash = previous.get("plan_hash")
    37 |     current_hash = current.get("plan_hash")
    38 |     plan_changed = previous_hash != current_hash
    39 |     return {
    40 |         "plan_changed": plan_changed,
    41 |         "plan_flip": plan_changed,
    42 |         "previous_plan_hash": previous_hash,
    43 |         "current_plan_hash": current_hash,
    44 |         "estimated_rows_delta": _number(current, "estimated_rows")
    45 |         - _number(previous, "estimated_rows"),
    46 |         "actual_rows_delta": _number(current, "actual_rows")
    47 |         - _number(previous, "actual_rows"),
    48 |         "actual_time_delta": _number(current, "actual_time")
    49 |         - _number(previous, "actual_time"),
    50 |         "previous_cardinality_error": calculate_cardinality_error(
    51 |             previous.get("estimated_rows"), previous.get("actual_rows")
    52 |         ),
    53 |         "current_cardinality_error": calculate_cardinality_error(
    54 |             current.get("estimated_rows"), current.get("actual_rows")
    55 |         ),
    56 |     }
    57 | 
    58 | 
    59 | def detect_plan_flip(previous: Mapping[str, Any], current: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
    60 |     """Return whether two plan snapshots have different non-null fingerprints."""
    61 |     return bool(diff_plans(previous, current)["plan_flip"])
    62 | 
    63 | 
    64 | def build_lock_graph(
    65 |     locks: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    66 |     activity: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None,
    67 | ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    68 |     """Build blocking edges from granted and waiting PostgreSQL locks.
    69 | 
    70 |     PostgreSQL's lock view does not always include a ``blocking_pid`` column;
    71 |     the relation/resource and granted state are sufficient to derive edges.
    72 |     Explicit blocking PIDs, when present in introspection output, are honored.
    73 |     Duplicate edges are removed while preserving input order.
    74 |     """
    75 |     del activity  # Activity is useful context, but lock compatibility is explicit here.
    76 |     holders: dict[Any, list[Any]] = defaultdict(list)
    77 |     for lock in locks:
    78 |         if lock.get("granted") and lock.get("relation") is not None:
    79 |             holders[lock["relation"]].append(lock.get("pid"))
    80 | 
    81 |     edges: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    82 |     seen: set[tuple[Any, Any, Any, Any]] = set()
    83 |     for lock in locks:
    84 |         if lock.get("granted") or lock.get("relation") is None:
    85 |             continue
    86 |         relation = lock["relation"]
    87 |         blocking_pids = (
    88 |             [lock["blocking_pid"]]
    89 |             if lock.get("blocking_pid") is not None
    90 |             else holders.get(relation, [])
    91 |         )
    92 |         for blocking_pid in blocking_pids:
    93 |             key = (blocking_pid, lock.get("pid"), relation, lock.get("mode"))
    94 |             if key in seen:
    95 |                 continue
    96 |             seen.add(key)
    97 |             edges.append(
    98 |                 {
    99 |                     "blocking_pid": blocking_pid,
   100 |                     "blocked_pid": lock.get("pid"),
   101 |                     "relation": relation,
   102 |                     "mode": lock.get("mode"),
   103 |                 }
   104 |             )
   105 |     return edges
   106 | 
   107 | 
   108 | def _as_datetime(value: Any) -> datetime | None:
   109 |     if value is None:
   110 |         return None
   111 |     if isinstance(value, datetime):
   112 |         return value if value.tzinfo else value.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
   113 |     if isinstance(value, str):
   114 |         parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
   115 |         return parsed if parsed.tzinfo else parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
   116 |     return None
   117 | 
   118 | 
   119 | def _age_seconds(now: datetime, value: Any) -> float | None:
   120 |     timestamp = _as_datetime(value)
   121 |     if timestamp is None:
   122 |         return None
   123 |     return max(0.0, (now - timestamp).total_seconds())
   124 | 
   125 | 
   126 | def calculate_vacuum_metrics(
   127 |     row: Mapping[str, Any],
   128 |     previous: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
   129 |     *,
   130 |     now: datetime | None = None,
   131 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
   132 |     """Calculate bloat, maintenance age, lag, and growth metrics for one row.
   133 | 
   134 |     Ages and rates are expressed in seconds and units per second respectively.
   135 |     Missing maintenance timestamps or an unavailable prior sample produce
   136 |     ``None`` rather than an invented value.
   137 |     """
   138 |     now = now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   139 |     if now.tzinfo is None:
   140 |         now = now.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
   141 | 
   142 |     live = max(_number(row, "live_tuples", "n_live_tup"), 0.0)
   143 |     dead = max(_number(row, "dead_tuples", "n_dead_tup"), 0.0)
   144 |     total = live + dead
   145 |     result = dict(row)
   146 |     result["dead_tuple_ratio"] = dead / total if total else 0.0
   147 |     vacuum_ages = [
   148 |         age for age in (
   149 |             _age_seconds(now, row.get("last_autovacuum")),
   150 |             _age_seconds(now, row.get("last_vacuum")),
   151 |         ) if age is not None
   152 |     ]
   153 |     analyze_ages = [
   154 |         age for age in (
   155 |             _age_seconds(now, row.get("last_autoanalyze")),
   156 |             _age_seconds(now, row.get("last_analyze")),
   157 |         ) if age is not None
   158 |     ]
   159 |     result["vacuum_age"] = min(vacuum_ages) if vacuum_ages else None
   160 |     result["analyze_age"] = min(analyze_ages) if analyze_ages else None
   161 |     result["autovacuum_lag"] = _age_seconds(now, row.get("last_autovacuum"))
   162 | 
   163 |     elapsed = None
   164 |     if previous is not None:
   165 |         current_time = _as_datetime(row.get("timestamp") or row.get("captured_at"))
   166 |         previous_time = _as_datetime(previous.get("timestamp") or previous.get("captured_at"))
   167 |         if current_time and previous_time:
   168 |             elapsed = (current_time - previous_time).total_seconds()
   169 |     if elapsed is None or elapsed <= 0 or previous is None:
   170 |         for key in ("table_size_bytes", "index_size_bytes", "row_count"):
   171 |             result[f"{key}_growth_rate"] = None
   172 |         result["table_growth_rate"] = None
   173 |         result["index_growth_rate"] = None
   174 |         result["row_growth_rate"] = None
   175 |     else:
   176 |         values = (
   177 |             ("table_size_bytes", ("table_size_bytes", "table_size"), "table_growth_rate"),
   178 |             ("index_size_bytes", ("index_size_bytes", "index_size"), "index_growth_rate"),
   179 |             ("row_count", ("row_count", "live_tuples", "n_live_tup"), "row_growth_rate"),
   180 |         )
   181 |         for output_key, keys, alias in values:
   182 |             current_value = _number(row, *keys)
   183 |             previous_value = _number(previous, *keys)
   184 |             rate = (current_value - previous_value) / elapsed
   185 |             result[f"{output_key}_growth_rate"] = rate
   186 |             result[alias] = rate
   187 |     return result
   188 | 
   189 | 
   190 | def compute_vacuum_metrics(
   191 |     rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
   192 |     *,
   193 |     now: datetime | None = None,
   194 | ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   195 |     """Compute vacuum metrics for chronologically ordered table snapshots."""
   196 |     previous_by_table: dict[tuple[Any, Any], Mapping[str, Any]] = {}
   197 |     result: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   198 |     for row in rows:
   199 |         key = (row.get("schema_name", row.get("schemaname")), row.get("table_name", row.get("relname")))
   200 |         metrics = calculate_vacuum_metrics(row, previous_by_table.get(key), now=now)
   201 |         result.append(metrics)
   202 |         previous_by_table[key] = row
   203 |     return result

     2 | 
     3 | from __future__ import annotations
     4 | 
     5 | import hashlib
     6 | import re
     7 | import uuid
     8 | from typing import Any
     9 |

    20 | 
    21 | _IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$")
    22 | _FROM_TABLE = re.compile(r"\b(?:from|join)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)", re.IGNORECASE)
    23 | _WHERE_COLUMN = re.compile(
    24 |     r"\bwhere\s+(?:[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\.)?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)\s*(?:=|>|<|\blike\b|\bin\b)\s*",
    25 |     re.IGNORECASE,
    26 | )
    27 | 
    28 | 
    29 | def _quoted_identifier(value: str | None) -> str | None:
    30 |     if not value or not _IDENTIFIER.fullmatch(value):
    31 |         return None
    32 |     # Identifiers are validated before interpolation; keeping them unquoted
    33 |     # also matches the strict candidate grammar used by the shadow executor.
    34 |     return value
    35 | 
    36 | 
    37 | def _candidate_from_query(query_text: str | None) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    38 |     if not query_text or "$" in query_text or ";" in query_text.rstrip(";"):
    39 |         return None
    40 |     table_match = _FROM_TABLE.search(query_text)
    41 |     column_match = _WHERE_COLUMN.search(query_text)
    42 |     table = _quoted_identifier(table_match.group(1) if table_match else None)
    43 |     column = _quoted_identifier(column_match.group(1) if column_match else None)
    44 |     if not table or not column:
    45 |         return None
    46 |     index_name = "zentrix_idx_" + hashlib.sha256(f"{table}:{column}".encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    47 |     return table, f"CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY {index_name} ON {table} ({column});"
    48 | 
    49 | 
    50 | async def _top_query(connection_id: uuid.UUID, db: AsyncSession) -> QueryMetric | None:
    51 |     statement = (
    52 |         select(QueryMetric)
    53 |         .where(
    54 |             QueryMetric.connection_id == connection_id,
    55 |             QueryMetric.query_text.is_not(None),
    56 |             or_(QueryMetric.query_text.ilike("select%"), QueryMetric.query_text.ilike("with%")),
    57 |         )
    58 |         .order_by(QueryMetric.total_exec_time.desc())
    59 |         .limit(1)
    60 |     )
    61 |     return await db.scalar(statement)
    62 | 
    63 | 
    64 | async def recommendations_for_diagnosis(
    65 |     diagnosis: Diagnosis,
    66 |     db: AsyncSession,
    67 | ) -> list[RecommendationOut]:
    68 |     """Build only actionable candidates supported by the diagnosis evidence."""
    69 |     cause = diagnosis.primary_root_cause.upper()
    70 |     plan: dict[str, Any] = diagnosis.validation_plan or {}
    71 |     affected = plan.get("affected_object")
    72 |     table = _quoted_identifier(str(affected).split(".")[-1] if affected not in {None, "database"} else None)
    73 | 
    74 |     candidate_type: str | None = None
    75 |     title: str | None = None
    76 |     candidate_sql: str | None = None
    77 |     predicted_impact: str | None = None
    78 |     risk = "Low"
    79 | 
    80 |     if cause in {"STALE_STATISTICS", "CARDINALITY_MISESTIMATION", "PLAN_FLIP"}:
    81 |         candidate_type = "STATISTICS"
    82 |         title = f"Refresh planner statistics{f' for {table}' if table else ''}"
    83 |         candidate_sql = f"ANALYZE {table};" if table else "ANALYZE;"
    84 |         predicted_impact = "May improve cardinality estimates and stabilize query plans."
    85 |     elif cause in {"VACUUM_LAG", "BLOAT"}:
    86 |         candidate_type = "VACUUM"
    87 |         title = f"Vacuum and analyze{f' {table}' if table else ' the affected relation'}"
    88 |         candidate_sql = f"VACUUM ANALYZE {table};" if table else None
    89 |         predicted_impact = "May reduce dead-tuple pressure and refresh planner statistics."
    90 |         risk = "Medium"
    91 |     elif cause == "INDEX_MISSING":
    92 |         query = await _top_query(diagnosis.connection_id, db)
    93 |         candidate = _candidate_from_query(query.query_text if query else None)
    94 |         if candidate:
    95 |             table, candidate_sql = candidate
    96 |             candidate_type = "INDEX"
    97 |             title = f"Add a selective index on {table}"
    98 |             predicted_impact = "May reduce sequential scans for the observed filtered workload."
    99 |             risk = "Medium"
   100 | 
   101 |     if not candidate_type or not title or not candidate_sql or not predicted_impact:
   102 |         return []
   103 | 
   104 |     recommendation_id = uuid.uuid5(
   105 |         uuid.NAMESPACE_URL,
   106 |         f"zentrix:recommendation:{diagnosis.id}:{candidate_sql}",
   107 |     )
   108 |     experiment = await db.scalar(
   109 |         select(OptimizationExperiment)
   110 |         .where(
   111 |             OptimizationExperiment.diagnosis_id == diagnosis.id,
   112 |             OptimizationExperiment.candidate_sql == candidate_sql,
   113 |         )
   114 |         .order_by(OptimizationExperiment.created_at.desc())
   115 |         .limit(1)
   116 |     )
   117 |     uncertainty = round(max(0.0, min(100.0, (1.0 - diagnosis.confidence) * 100.0)), 1)
   118 |     return [
   119 |         RecommendationOut(
   120 |             id=recommendation_id,
   121 |             diagnosis_id=diagnosis.id,
   122 |             connection_id=diagnosis.connection_id,
   123 |             diagnosis_title=diagnosis.title,
   124 |             primary_root_cause=cause,
   125 |             type=candidate_type,
   126 |             title=title,
   127 |             rationale=(
   128 |                 f"Generated from the persisted {cause} diagnosis and its live PostgreSQL evidence. "
   129 |                 "The candidate must pass shadow replay and policy verification before approval."
   130 |             ),
   131 |             predicted_impact=predicted_impact,
   132 |             uncertainty_pct=uncertainty,
   133 |             risk=risk,
   134 |             candidate_sql=candidate_sql,
   135 |             experiment_id=experiment.id if experiment else None,
   136 |         )
   137 |     ]
   138 | 
   139 | 
   140 | async def recommendations_for_connection(
   141 |     connection_id: uuid.UUID | None,
   142 |     db: AsyncSession,
   143 | ) -> list[RecommendationOut]:
   144 |     statement = select(Diagnosis).order_by(Diagnosis.created_at.desc())
   145 |     if connection_id:
   146 |         statement = statement.where(Diagnosis.connection_id == connection_id)
   147 |     diagnoses = (await db.scalars(statement)).all()
   148 |     recommendations: list[RecommendationOut] = []
   149 |     for diagnosis in diagnoses:
   150 |         recommendations.extend(await recommendations_for_diagnosis(diagnosis, db))
   151 |     return recommendations

   113 |             "io_savings_usd": 0.0,
   114 |             "assumed_pricing_tier": pricing_tier,
   115 |             "is_cost_model_configured": False,
   116 |             "calculation_details": {
   117 |                 "status": "COST_MODEL_NOT_CONFIGURED",
   118 |                 "message": f"Pricing tier '{pricing_tier}' has no configured pricing parameters.",
   119 |             },
   120 |         }
   121 | 
   122 |     monthly_calls = max(0.0, frequency_per_day) * DAYS_PER_MONTH
   123 | 
   124 |     # 1. Compute savings
   125 |     delta_cpu = max(0.0, baseline_cpu_seconds - candidate_cpu_seconds)
   126 |     compute_savings = (delta_cpu * monthly_calls * (cpu_rate / 3600.0))
   127 | 
   128 |     # 2. IO savings
   129 |     delta_io = max(0.0, baseline_io_reads - candidate_io_reads)
   130 |     io_savings = (delta_io * monthly_calls * (io_rate / 1_000_000.0))

   132 |     # 3. Storage overhead
   133 |     storage_gb = max(0.0, index_storage_mb) / 1024.0
   134 |     storage_cost = storage_gb * storage_rate
   135 | 
   136 |     # Total savings
   137 |     total_savings = round(max(0.0, compute_savings + io_savings - storage_cost), 2)

   139 |     io_rounded = round(io_savings, 2)
   140 |     storage_rounded = round(storage_cost, 2)

45 | async def _load_replay_workload(
    46 |     connection_id: uuid.UUID,
    47 |     db: AsyncSession,
    48 |     query_id: int | None = None,
    49 | ) -> list[ReplayQuery]:
    50 |     """Load executable read queries from the live target for shadow replay."""
    51 |     pool = await customer_connection_manager.get_customer_pool(connection_id, db)
    52 |     async with pool.acquire() as customer:
    53 |         rows = await get_query_metrics(customer, limit=100)
    54 | 
    55 |     workload: list[ReplayQuery] = []
    56 |     seen: set[str] = set()
    57 |     for row in rows:
    58 |         if query_id is not None and row.get("queryid") != query_id:
    59 |             continue
    60 |         query = str(row.get("query") or "").strip()
    61 |         normalized = query.rstrip(";").strip()
    62 |         if (
    63 |             not normalized
    64 |             or ";" in normalized
    65 |             or not normalized.lower().startswith(("select", "with"))
    66 |             or "$" in normalized
    67 |             or normalized in seen
    68 |         ):
    69 |             continue
    70 |         seen.add(normalized)
    71 |         workload.append(ReplayQuery(query=normalized, weight=max(1, min(int(row.get("calls") or 1), 3))))
    72 |         if len(workload) >= 25:
    73 |             break
    74 | 
    75 |     if not workload:
    76 |         raise ValueError("No replayable parameter-free read queries were found in pg_stat_statements")
    77 |     return workload

     3 | Provides session-local hypothetical index creation, drops, and planner-cost
     4 | evaluations using the PostgreSQL `hypopg` extension.
     5 | 
     6 | Results are explicitly labeled as PLANNER_COST_SIGNAL, per PRD.md §5 and
     7 | TECHSTACK.md, to clearly distinguish planner estimates from verified runtime
     8 | performance.

   123 | def _extract_plan_cost_and_indexes(plan_payload: Any) -> tuple[float, list[str]]:
   124 |     """Extract total estimated cost and index names used from EXPLAIN JSON."""
   125 |     root = plan_payload
   126 |     if isinstance(plan_payload, list) and plan_payload:
   127 |         root = plan_payload[0].get("Plan", plan_payload[0]) if isinstance(plan_payload[0], dict) else plan_payload[0]
   128 |     if isinstance(root, dict) and "Plan" in root:
   129 |         root = root["Plan"]
   130 |     if not isinstance(root, dict):
   131 |         return 0.0, []
   132 | 
   133 |     total_cost = float(root.get("Total Cost") or root.get("total_cost") or 0.0)
   134 |     used_indexes: list[str] = []
   135 |     stack = [root]
   136 |     while stack:
   137 |         node = stack.pop()
   138 |         index_name = node.get("Index Name") or node.get("index_name")
   139 |         if index_name:
   140 |             used_indexes.append(str(index_name))
   141 |         stack.extend(node.get("Plans") or [])
   142 |     return total_cost, used_indexes

143 | 
   144 | 
   145 | async def evaluate_hypothetical_index(
   146 |     connection: asyncpg.Connection,
   147 |     query: str,
   148 |     index_statement: str,
   149 |     *query_args: Any,
   150 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
   151 |     """Compare baseline planner cost vs. cost with a hypothetical index.
   152 | 
   153 |     Cleans up the hypothetical index upon completion and attaches an explicit
   154 |     disclaimer stating that planner cost is a theoretical estimate, not a
   155 |     proven runtime latency reduction.
   156 |     """
   157 |     valid_query = _validate_read_query(query)
   158 |     valid_index_stmt = validate_index_statement(index_statement)
   159 | 
   160 |     # 1. Baseline explain
   161 |     baseline_records = await connection.fetch(
   162 |         f"EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) {valid_query}", *query_args
   163 |     )
   164 |     baseline_plan = baseline_records[0][0] if baseline_records else {}
   165 |     baseline_cost, baseline_indexes = _extract_plan_cost_and_indexes(baseline_plan)
   166 | 
   167 |     # 2. Create hypothetical index
   168 |     hypo_info = await create_hypothetical_index(connection, valid_index_stmt)
   169 |     index_relid = hypo_info["indexrelid"]
   170 |     hypo_index_name = hypo_info["indexname"]
   171 | 
   172 |     try:
   173 |         # 3. Candidate explain with hypothetical index active
   174 |         candidate_records = await connection.fetch(
   175 |             f"EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) {valid_query}", *query_args
   176 |         )
   177 |         candidate_plan = candidate_records[0][0] if candidate_records else {}
   178 |         candidate_cost, candidate_indexes = _extract_plan_cost_and_indexes(candidate_plan)
   179 |     finally:
   180 |         # 4. Ensure cleanup
   181 |         await drop_hypothetical_index(connection, index_relid)
   182 | 
   183 |     cost_delta = candidate_cost - baseline_cost
   184 |     cost_reduction_ratio = (
   185 |         (baseline_cost - candidate_cost) / max(baseline_cost, 1e-6)
   186 |         if baseline_cost > 0
   187 |         else 0.0
   188 |     )
   189 |     index_used = (
   190 |         hypo_index_name in candidate_indexes
   191 |         or any(str(index_relid) in idx for idx in candidate_indexes)
   192 |         or (candidate_cost < baseline_cost)
   193 |     )
   194 | 
   195 |     return {
   196 |         "candidate_statement": valid_index_stmt,
   197 |         "query": valid_query,
   198 |         "baseline_cost": baseline_cost,
   199 |         "candidate_cost": candidate_cost,
   200 |         "cost_delta": cost_delta,
   201 |         "cost_reduction_ratio": max(0.0, min(cost_reduction_ratio, 1.0)),
   202 |         "index_used": index_used,
   203 |         "is_improvement": bool(cost_reduction_ratio > 0 and index_used),
   204 |         "baseline_indexes": baseline_indexes,
   205 |         "candidate_indexes": candidate_indexes,
   206 |         "signal_type": "PLANNER_COST_SIGNAL",
   207 |         "is_verified_performance": False,
   208 |         "disclaimer": (
   209 |             "Planner cost estimates from HypoPG are theoretical signals only, "
   210 |             "not verified runtime performance. Candidate must undergo shadow database "
   211 |             "replay and paired statistical verification before deployment."
   212 |         ),
   213 |     }

   216 | async def filter_candidates(
   217 |     connection: asyncpg.Connection,
   218 |     query: str,
   219 |     candidate_statements: Sequence[str],
   220 |     *,
   221 |     top_k: int = 10,
   222 |     min_cost_reduction: float = 0.05,
   223 |     query_args: Sequence[Any] | None = None,
   224 | ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   225 |     """Fast-filter multiple candidate index statements using HypoPG.
   226 | 
   227 |     Reduces large sets of candidate indexes down to the top K viable options
   228 |     based on planner cost reduction.
   229 |     """
   230 |     args = query_args or ()
   231 |     results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   232 | 
   233 |     for statement in candidate_statements:
   234 |         try:
   235 |             eval_res = await evaluate_hypothetical_index(
   236 |                 connection, query, statement, *args
   237 |             )
   238 |             if eval_res["is_improvement"] and eval_res["cost_reduction_ratio"] >= min_cost_reduction:

   240 |         except Exception as exc:

   242 |                 f"Candidate evaluation failed for {statement!r}: {exc}"
   243 |             )
   244 | 
   245 |     # Sort descending by cost reduction ratio
   246 |     results.sort(key=lambda item: item["cost_reduction_ratio"], reverse=True)
   247 |     return results[:top_k]

     3 | This module is the only customer-database boundary used by diagnosis and

     5 | supplied values are bound parameters and identifiers are validated before

    22 | _READ_QUERY = re.compile(r"^(select|with)\b", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
    23 | _WRITE_KEYWORDS = re.compile(

   226 | def build_lock_graph(locks: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   227 |     holders = defaultdict(list)
   228 |     for lock in locks:
   229 |         if lock.get("granted") and lock.get("relation") is not None:
   230 |             holders[lock["relation"]].append(lock.get("pid"))
   231 |     edges = []
   232 |     for lock in locks:
   233 |         if lock.get("granted") or lock.get("relation") is None:
   234 |             continue
   235 |         for holder in holders[lock["relation"]]:
   236 |             edges.append({"blocking_pid": holder, "blocked_pid": lock.get("pid"), "relation": lock["relation"], "mode": lock.get("mode")})
   237 |     return edges

chunk_01ae81e3bc5ec787.numbered_code:
1 | """Deterministic Policy Engine for guarded optimization deployment.
     2 | 
     3 | Evaluates simulation and verification results against hard, non-overridable
     4 | safety and performance thresholds before canary deployment or user approval.
     5 | 
     6 | Independent of LLM judgments per ARCHITECTURE.md §4, §8 & PRD.md §5 Feature 2.
     7 | """
     8 | 
     9 | from __future__ import annotations
    10 | 
    11 | from collections.abc import Mapping
    12 | from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
    13 | from datetime import datetime, timezone
    14 | from typing import Any
    15 | 
    16 | 
    17 | @dataclass
    18 | class PolicyConfig:
    19 |     """Configurable threshold parameters for deterministic deployment gating."""
    20 | 
    21 |     min_p95_improvement_ratio: float = 0.10  # >= 10% p95 latency reduction
    22 |     require_ci_excludes_zero: bool = True  # CI upper bound must be < 0
    23 |     max_regression_rate: float = 0.05  # <= 5% of workload queries regressed
    24 |     max_write_latency_increase_ratio: float = 0.15  # <= 15% write latency increase
    25 |     max_storage_increase_ratio: float = 0.20  # <= 20% storage/index growth
    26 |     max_skeptic_score: float = 0.40  # Skeptic adversarial risk score < 0.40
    27 |     min_sample_size: int = 10  # Minimum paired workload observations
    28 | 
    29 | 
    30 | def _number(mapping: Mapping[str, Any], *keys: str, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
    31 |     for key in keys:
    32 |         val = mapping.get(key)
    33 |         if val is not None:
    34 |             try:
    35 |                 return float(val)
    36 |             except (ValueError, TypeError):
    37 |                 continue
    38 |     return default
    39 | 
    40 | 
    41 | def evaluate(
    42 |     verification_result: Mapping[str, Any],
    43 |     config: PolicyConfig | None = None,
    44 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    45 |     """Evaluate simulation/verification metrics against deterministic safety rules.
    46 | 
    47 |     Returns a structured PolicyVerdict dict with APPROVE, BLOCK, or CONDITIONAL.
    48 |     """
    49 |     cfg = config or PolicyConfig()
    50 |     passed_rules: list[str] = []
    51 |     violated_rules: list[str] = []
    52 | 
    53 |     # 1. Sample Size / Statistical Power Check
    54 |     sample_size = int(_number(verification_result, "sample_size", "paired_samples", default=0))
    55 |     is_underpowered = sample_size > 0 and sample_size < cfg.min_sample_size
    56 |     if is_underpowered:
    57 |         violated_rules.append(
    58 |             f"Sample size ({sample_size}) is below minimum required ({cfg.min_sample_size})"
    59 |         )
    60 |     else:
    61 |         passed_rules.append("statistical_sample_size")
    62 | 
    63 |     # 2. P95 Latency Improvement Check
    64 |     baseline_p95 = _number(verification_result, "baseline_p95", "p95_baseline")
    65 |     candidate_p95 = _number(verification_result, "candidate_p95", "p95_candidate")
    66 |     p95_improvement = _number(
    67 |         verification_result,
    68 |         "p95_improvement_ratio",
    69 |         "p95_improvement",
    70 |         default=(
    71 |             (baseline_p95 - candidate_p95) / max(baseline_p95, 1e-6)
    72 |             if baseline_p95 > 0
    73 |             else 0.0
    74 |         ),
    75 |     )
    76 |     if p95_improvement < cfg.min_p95_improvement_ratio:
    77 |         violated_rules.append(
    78 |             f"p95 improvement ({p95_improvement:.1%}) below required threshold ({cfg.min_p95_improvement_ratio:.1%})"
    79 |         )
    80 |     else:
    81 |         passed_rules.append("p95_improvement")
    82 | 
    83 |     # 3. Bootstrap Confidence Interval Check (excludes zero / upper < 0)
    84 |     ci_upper = _number(verification_result, "ci_upper", "ci_high", "ci_95_upper", default=0.0)
    85 |     ci_excludes_zero = verification_result.get("ci_excludes_zero")
    86 |     if ci_excludes_zero is None:
    87 |         ci_excludes_zero = ci_upper < 0.0 or (p95_improvement >= cfg.min_p95_improvement_ratio and sample_size >= cfg.min_sample_size)
    88 |     if cfg.require_ci_excludes_zero and not bool(ci_excludes_zero):
    89 |         violated_rules.append("Bootstrap confidence interval does not exclude zero")
    90 |     else:
    91 |         passed_rules.append("confidence_interval_excludes_zero")
    92 | 
    93 |     # 4. Query Regression Rate Check
    94 |     regression_rate = _number(verification_result, "regression_rate", default=0.0)
    95 |     if regression_rate > cfg.max_regression_rate:
    96 |         violated_rules.append(
    97 |             f"Workload regression rate ({regression_rate:.1%}) exceeds threshold ({cfg.max_regression_rate:.1%})"
    98 |         )
    99 |     else:
   100 |         passed_rules.append("regression_rate")
   101 | 
   102 |     # 5. Write Latency / DML Degradation Check
   103 |     write_increase = _number(
   104 |         verification_result,
   105 |         "write_latency_increase_ratio",
   106 |         "write_latency_delta",
   107 |         "write_amplification",
   108 |         default=0.0,
   109 |     )
   110 |     if write_increase > cfg.max_write_latency_increase_ratio:
   111 |         violated_rules.append(
   112 |             f"Write latency increase ({write_increase:.1%}) exceeds threshold ({cfg.max_write_latency_increase_ratio:.1%})"
   113 |         )
   114 |     else:
   115 |         passed_rules.append("write_latency_overhead")
   116 | 
   117 |     # 6. Storage Growth Check
   118 |     storage_increase = _number(
   119 |         verification_result,
   120 |         "storage_increase_ratio",
   121 |         "storage_delta",
   122 |         "index_size_ratio",
   123 |         default=0.0,
   124 |     )
   125 |     if storage_increase > cfg.max_storage_increase_ratio:
   126 |         violated_rules.append(
   127 |             f"Storage growth ({storage_increase:.1%}) exceeds threshold ({cfg.max_storage_increase_ratio:.1%})"
   128 |         )
   129 |     else:
   130 |         passed_rules.append("storage_growth")
   131 | 
   132 |     # 7. Skeptic Agent Adversarial Risk Score Check
   133 |     skeptic_score = _number(
   134 |         verification_result,
   135 |         "skeptic_score",
   136 |         "skeptic_risk_score",
   137 |         "risk_score",
   138 |         default=0.0,
   139 |     )

   215 |         "pg_dump",
   216 |         "--format=custom",
   217 |         "--no-owner",
   218 |         "--no-acl",
   219 |         "--dbname",
   220 |         source_dsn,
   221 |         stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
   222 |         stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
   223 |     )
   224 |     restore = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
   225 |         "pg_restore",
   226 |         "--no-owner",
   227 |         "--no-acl",

   282 | async def clone_schema_and_tables(
   283 |     source_conn: asyncpg.Connection,
   284 |     target_conn: asyncpg.Connection,
   285 |     table_names: Sequence[str],
   286 |     *,
   287 |     sample_limit: int | None = None,
   288 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
   289 |     """Lightweight in-Python table cloner for test fixtures or sampled shadow runs."""
   290 |     cloned_tables = []
   291 |     for table in table_names:
   292 |         # Get column definitions
   293 |         cols = await source_conn.fetch(
   294 |             """
   295 |             SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable
   296 |             FROM information_schema.columns
   297 |             WHERE table_name = $1
   298 |             ORDER BY ordinal_position
   299 |             """,
   300 |             table,
   301 |         )
   302 |         if not cols:
   303 |             continue
   304 | 
   305 |         col_defs = ", ".join(f'"{c["column_name"]}" {c["data_type"]}' for c in cols)
   306 |         await target_conn.execute(f'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "{table}" ({col_defs})')
   307 | 
   308 |         # Copy data
   309 |         limit_clause = f" LIMIT {sample_limit}" if sample_limit else ""
   310 |         rows = await source_conn.fetch(f'SELECT * FROM "{table}"{limit_clause}')
   311 |         if rows:
   312 |             col_names = [f'"{c["column_name"]}"' for c in cols]
   313 |             placeholders = ", ".join(f"${i+1}" for i in range(len(col_names)))
   314 |             insert_sql = f'INSERT INTO "{table}" ({", ".join(col_names)}) VALUES ({placeholders})'
   315 |             for row in rows:
   316 |                 await target_conn.execute(insert_sql, *row.values())
   317 | 
   318 |         cloned_tables.append(table)
   319 | 
   320 |     return {"status": "CLONED", "tables": cloned_tables, "sample_limit": sample_limit}

1 | """Unified CLI Dispatcher for Zentrix Background Workers.
     2 | 
     3 | Enables a single container image (worker.Dockerfile) to run any of the four
     4 | independent worker processes via command-line argument:
     5 | - telemetry: app.workers.telemetry_collector
     6 | - canary: app.workers.canary_monitor
     7 | - retrain: app.workers.retrain_worker
     8 | - shadow: app.workers.shadow_lab_worker
     9 | 
    10 | Reference: ARCHITECTURE.md §4, §6 & PRD.md §13.
    11 | """
    12 | 
    13 | from __future__ import annotations
    14 | 
    15 | import argparse
    16 | import asyncio
    17 | import sys
    18 | 
    19 | from app.core.logging import get_logger
    20 | 
    21 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
    22 | 
    23 | 
    24 | def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    25 |     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
    26 |         description="Zentrix Background Worker Process Runner",
    27 |         formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter,
    28 |     )
    29 |     parser.add_argument(
    30 |         "worker_type",
    31 |         choices=["telemetry", "canary", "retrain", "shadow"],
    32 |         help="Type of background worker process to run",
    33 |     )
    34 |     parser.add_argument(
    35 |         "--interval",
    36 |         type=int,
    37 |         default=None,
    38 |         help="Custom polling interval in seconds",
    39 |     )
    40 |     return parser.parse_args()
    41 | 
    42 | 
    43 | async def run_selected_worker(worker_type: str, interval: int | None = None) -> None:
    44 |     """Dispatch to selected worker main loop."""
    45 |     logger.info(f"Launching Zentrix worker process: '{worker_type}'")
    46 | 
    47 |     if worker_type == "telemetry":
    48 |         from app.workers.telemetry_collector import main as telemetry_main
    49 |         await telemetry_main()
    50 |     elif worker_type == "canary":
    51 |         from app.workers.canary_monitor import main as canary_main
    52 |         await canary_main()
    53 |     elif worker_type == "retrain":
    54 |         from app.workers.retrain_worker import main as retrain_main
    55 |         await retrain_main()
    56 |     elif worker_type == "shadow":
    57 |         from app.workers.shadow_lab_worker import main as shadow_main
    58 |         await shadow_main()
    59 |     else:
    60 |         logger.error(f"Unknown worker type: {worker_type}")
    61 |         sys.exit(1)
    62 | 
    63 | 
    64 | def main() -> None:
    65 |     args = parse_args()
    66 |     try:
    67 |         asyncio.run(run_selected_worker(args.worker_type, args.interval))
    68 |     except KeyboardInterrupt:
    69 |         logger.info(f"Worker '{args.worker_type}' shutting down cleanly on SIGINT")
    70 | 
    71 | 
    72 | if __name__ == "__main__":
    73 |     main()

   113 | def generate_rollback_sql(canary_sql: str) -> str:
   114 |     """Generate the safe rollback SQL statement for an applied canary action."""
   115 |     cleaned = canary_sql.strip()
   116 |     upper = cleaned.upper()
   117 |     if "CREATE INDEX" in upper or "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX" in upper:
   118 |         # Extract index name
   119 |         import re
   120 |         match = re.search(r"INDEX\s+(?:CONCURRENTLY\s+)?(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?([A-Za-z0-9_$]+)", cleaned, re.IGNORECASE)
   121 |         if match:
   122 |             idx_name = match.group(1)
   123 |             return f"DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS {idx_name}"
   124 |     return "/* ROLLBACK ACTION NOT REQUIRED */"

42 | async def compute_prediction_errors_and_calibration(
    43 |     db: AsyncSession,
    44 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    45 |     """Compute prediction errors (MAE, RMSE) and calibration coverage across 5 confidence buckets."""
    46 |     # Query all predictions joined with their experiments
    47 |     stmt = (
    48 |         select(ModelPrediction)
    49 |         .options(selectinload(ModelPrediction.experiment))
    50 |         .order_by(ModelPrediction.created_at.desc())
    51 |     )
    52 |     result = await db.execute(stmt)
    53 |     predictions = list(result.scalars().all())
    54 | 
    55 |     if not predictions:
    56 |         return {
    57 |             "total_labeled": 0,
    58 |             "mae": 0.0,
    59 |             "rmse": 0.0,
    60 |             "calibration_error": 0.0,
    61 |             "calibration_report": [],
    62 |             "models": {},
    63 |         }
    64 | 
    65 |     version_errors: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
    66 |     version_squared_errors: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
    67 |     bucket_counts: dict[str, int] = {f"{low:.1f}-{high:.1f}": 0 for low, high in CALIBRATION_BUCKETS}
    68 |     bucket_hits: dict[str, int] = {f"{low:.1f}-{high:.1f}": 0 for low, high in CALIBRATION_BUCKETS}
    69 | 
    70 |     all_abs_errors: list[float] = []
    71 |     all_sq_errors: list[float] = []
    72 | 
    73 |     for pred in predictions:
    74 |         exp = pred.experiment
    75 |         if exp is None:
    76 |             continue
    77 | 
    78 |         # Actual delta observed from experiment (candidate_p95 - baseline_p95)
    79 |         actual_delta = exp.candidate_p95 - exp.baseline_p95
    80 |         abs_err = abs(actual_delta - pred.prediction)
    81 |         sq_err = (actual_delta - pred.prediction) ** 2
    82 | 
    83 |         # Update prediction record if not populated
    84 |         if pred.actual is None or pred.absolute_error is None:
    85 |             pred.actual = actual_delta
    86 |             pred.absolute_error = abs_err
    87 |             exp.actual_latency_delta = actual_delta
    88 |             exp.prediction_error = abs_err
    89 | 
    90 |         v = pred.model_version or "v1"
    91 |         version_errors.setdefault(v, []).append(abs_err)
    92 |         version_squared_errors.setdefault(v, []).append(sq_err)
    93 |         all_abs_errors.append(abs_err)
    94 |         all_sq_errors.append(sq_err)
    95 | 
    96 |         # Calibration tracking: does the interval [lower_bound, upper_bound] cover actual outcome?
    97 |         conf = float(np.clip(pred.confidence, 0.0, 1.0))
    98 |         is_covered = pred.lower_bound <= actual_delta <= pred.upper_bound
    99 | 
   100 |         for low, high in CALIBRATION_BUCKETS:
   101 |             if (low <= conf < high) or (high == 1.0 and conf == 1.0):
   102 |                 b_name = f"{low:.1f}-{high:.1f}"
   103 |                 bucket_counts[b_name] += 1
   104 |                 if is_covered:
   105 |                     bucket_hits[b_name] += 1
   106 |                 break
   107 | 
   108 |     await db.commit()
   109 | 
   110 |     # Build calibration table across >=5 buckets per PRD §21
   111 |     calibration_report: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   112 |     total_n = len(all_abs_errors)
   113 |     ece = 0.0
   114 | 
   115 |     for low, high in CALIBRATION_BUCKETS:
   116 |         b_name = f"{low:.1f}-{high:.1f}"
   117 |         cnt = bucket_counts[b_name]
   118 |         mid_conf = (low + high) / 2.0
   119 |         emp_coverage = (bucket_hits[b_name] / cnt) if cnt > 0 else mid_conf
   120 | 
   121 |         if cnt > 0 and total_n > 0:
   122 |             ece += (cnt / total_n) * abs(mid_conf - emp_coverage)
   123 | 
   124 |         calibration_report.append({
   125 |             "bucket": b_name,
   126 |             "predicted_confidence": float(mid_conf),
   127 |             "empirical_coverage": float(emp_coverage),
   128 |             "sample_count": cnt,
   129 |         })
   130 | 
   131 |     model_metrics: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
   132 |     for v, errs in version_errors.items():
   133 |         sq_errs = version_squared_errors.get(v, errs)
   134 |         model_metrics[v] = {
   135 |             "mae": float(np.mean(errs)),
   136 |             "rmse": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(sq_errs))),
   137 |             "count": len(errs),
   138 |         }
   139 | 
   140 |     return {
   141 |         "total_labeled": len(all_abs_errors),
   142 |         "mae": float(np.mean(all_abs_errors)) if all_abs_errors else 0.0,
   143 |         "rmse": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(all_sq_errors))) if all_sq_errors else 0.0,
   144 |         "expected_calibration_error": float(ece),
   145 |         "calibration_report": calibration_report,
   146 |         "models": model_metrics,
   147 |     }

   150 | def compute_feature_drift_score(
   151 |     reference: Sequence[float],
   152 |     current: Sequence[float],
   153 | ) -> float:
   154 |     """Compute two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov drift score between reference and current samples."""
   155 |     if len(reference) < 5 or len(current) < 5:
   156 |         return 0.0
   157 | 
   158 |     # KS statistic D in [0, 1]
   159 |     res = stats.ks_2samp(reference, current)
   160 |     return float(res.statistic)

   172 |     ref_stmt = select(OptimizationExperiment).where(OptimizationExperiment.timestamp < split_time).limit(100)
   173 |     curr_stmt = select(OptimizationExperiment).where(OptimizationExperiment.timestamp >= split_time).limit(100)
   174 |

   176 |     curr_res = await db.execute(curr_stmt)

   179 |     curr_exps = list(curr_res.scalars().all())
   180 |

   182 | 
   183 |     for feat in ["baseline_p95", "candidate_p95", "baseline_cpu", "baseline_io"]:
   184 |         ref_vals = [float(getattr(e, feat, 0.0)) for e in ref_exps]
   185 |         curr_vals = [float(getattr(e, feat, 0.0)) for e in curr_exps]
   186 |         score = compute_feature_drift_score(ref_vals, curr_vals)

   188 |

   191 |     curr_preds = [float(e.predicted_latency_delta) for e in curr_exps]
   192 |     pred_drift_score = compute_feature_drift_score(ref_preds, curr_preds)

   195 |     is_drift = bool(dataset_drift_score >= drift_threshold or pred_drift_score >= drift_threshold)

   210 |     )

   213 |     await db.refresh(report)

    43 |     connection: asyncpg.Connection,
    44 |     query: str,
    45 |     *args: Any,
    46 | ) -> tuple[float, bool, str | None]:
    47 |     """Execute a single query and measure wall-clock latency in milliseconds."""
    48 |     start = time.perf_counter()
    49 |     try:
    50 |         await connection.fetch(query, *args)
    51 |         duration_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000.0
    52 |         return duration_ms, True, None
    53 |     except Exception as exc:

    57 | 
    58 | async def replay_workload(
    59 |     connection: asyncpg.Connection,
    60 |     workload: Sequence[ReplayQuery | Mapping[str, Any] | str],
    61 |     *,
    62 |     iterations: int = 1,
    63 | ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    64 |     """Replay a sequence of queries against a database connection and capture latency."""
    65 |     latencies: list[float] = []
    66 |     read_latencies: list[float] = []
    67 |     write_latencies: list[float] = []
    68 |     errors: list[str] = []
    69 | 
    70 |     for _ in range(max(1, iterations)):
    71 |         for item in workload:
    72 |             if isinstance(item, str):
    73 |                 q, args, is_write = item, (), False
    74 |             elif isinstance(item, ReplayQuery):
    75 |                 q, args, is_write = item.query, item.args, item.is_write
    76 |             elif isinstance(item, Mapping):
    77 |                 q = item.get("query", "")
    78 |                 args = item.get("args", item.get("parameters", ()))
    79 |                 is_write = bool(item.get("is_write", False))
    80 |             else:
    81 |                 continue
    82 | 
    83 |             for _ in range(max(1, int(item.weight) if isinstance(item, ReplayQuery) else 1)):
    84 |                 lat, success, err = await _execute_timed(connection, q, *args)
    85 |                 if success:
    86 |                     latencies.append(lat)
    87 |                     if is_write:
    88 |                         write_latencies.append(lat)
    89 |                     else:
    90 |                         read_latencies.append(lat)
    91 |                 else:
    92 |                     errors.append(err or "Unknown query error")
    93 | 
    94 |     if not latencies:
    95 |         return {
    96 |             "p50_ms": 0.0,
    97 |             "p95_ms": 0.0,
    98 |             "p99_ms": 0.0,
    99 |             "mean_ms": 0.0,
   100 |             "sample_count": 0,
   101 |             "latencies": [],
   102 |             "write_mean_ms": 0.0,
   103 |             "error_rate": 1.0 if errors else 0.0,
   104 |             "errors": errors,
   105 |         }
   106 | 
   107 |     arr = np.asarray(latencies, dtype=np.float64)
   108 |     return {
   109 |         "p50_ms": float(np.percentile(arr, 50)),
   110 |         "p95_ms": float(np.percentile(arr, 95)),
   111 |         "p99_ms": float(np.percentile(arr, 99)),
   112 |         "mean_ms": float(np.mean(arr)),
   113 |         "sample_count": len(arr),
   114 |         "latencies": latencies,
   115 |         "write_mean_ms": float(np.mean(write_latencies)) if write_latencies else 0.0,
   116 |         "error_rate": len(errors) / max(len(latencies) + len(errors), 1),
   117 |         "errors": errors,
   118 |     }

   121 | class ShadowLabWorker:
   122 |     """Worker managing paired simulation runs against shadow or test databases."""
   123 | 
   124 |     async def run_simulation_experiment(
   125 |         self,
   126 |         target_connection: asyncpg.Connection,
   127 |         candidate_sql: str,
   128 |         workload: Sequence[ReplayQuery | Mapping[str, Any] | str],
   129 |         *,
   130 |         iterations: int = 1,
   131 |     ) -> dict[str, Any]:
   132 |         """Execute paired baseline vs candidate simulation on a connection."""
   133 |         before_size = await target_connection.fetchval("SELECT pg_database_size(current_database())")
   134 | 
   135 |         # 1. Baseline workload replay
   136 |         baseline_metrics = await replay_workload(target_connection, workload, iterations=iterations)
   137 | 
   138 |         # 2. Install candidate optimization
   139 |         install_res = await install_candidate_optimization(target_connection, candidate_sql)
   140 |         if not install_res["success"]:
   141 |             return {
   142 |                 "status": "FAILED",
   143 |                 "candidate_sql": candidate_sql,
   144 |                 "error": install_res["error"],
   145 |                 "baseline_metrics": baseline_metrics,
   146 |                 "candidate_metrics": None,
   147 |             }
   148 | 
   149 |         # 3. Candidate workload replay
   150 |         candidate_metrics = await replay_workload(target_connection, workload, iterations=iterations)
   151 | 
   152 |         # 4. Paired delta calculation
   153 |         base_lats = baseline_metrics["latencies"]
   154 |         cand_lats = candidate_metrics["latencies"]
   155 |         paired_count = min(len(base_lats), len(cand_lats))
   156 | 
   157 |         regressions = sum(1 for i in range(paired_count) if cand_lats[i] > base_lats[i])
   158 |         regression_rate = regressions / max(paired_count, 1)
   159 | 
   160 |         base_p95 = baseline_metrics["p95_ms"]
   161 |         cand_p95 = candidate_metrics["p95_ms"]
   162 |         p95_improvement = (base_p95 - cand_p95) / max(base_p95, 1e-6) if base_p95 > 0 else 0.0
   163 | 
   164 |         base_write = baseline_metrics["write_mean_ms"]
   165 |         cand_write = candidate_metrics["write_mean_ms"]
   166 |         write_increase = (
   167 |             (cand_write - base_write) / max(base_write, 1e-6)
   168 |             if base_write > 0 and cand_write > 0
   169 |             else 0.0
   170 |         )
   171 | 
   172 |         after_size = await target_connection.fetchval("SELECT pg_database_size(current_database())")
   173 |         storage_increase = (
   174 |             max(0.0, (float(after_size) - float(before_size)) / max(float(before_size), 1.0))
   175 |             if before_size is not None and after_size is not None
   176 |             else 0.0
   177 |         )
   178 | 
   179 |         return {
   180 |             "status": "COMPLETED",
   181 |             "candidate_sql": candidate_sql,
   182 |             "install_duration_ms": install_res["duration_ms"],
   183 |             "sample_size": paired_count,
   184 |             "baseline_p50": baseline_metrics["p50_ms"],
   185 |             "baseline_p95": base_p95,
   186 |             "baseline_p99": baseline_metrics["p99_ms"],
   187 |             "candidate_p50": candidate_metrics["p50_ms"],
   188 |             "candidate_p95": cand_p95,
   189 |             "candidate_p99": candidate_metrics["p99_ms"],
   190 |             "p95_improvement_ratio": float(p95_improvement),
   191 |             "regression_rate": float(regression_rate),
   192 |             "write_latency_increase_ratio": float(max(0.0, write_increase)),
   193 |             "storage_increase_ratio": float(storage_increase),
   194 |             "baseline_metrics": baseline_metrics,
   195 |             "candidate_metrics": candidate_metrics,
   196 |         }
   197 | 
   198 |     async def run_ephemeral_experiment(
   199 |         self,
   200 |         source_dsn: str,
   201 |         candidate_sql: str,
   202 |         workload: Sequence[ReplayQuery | Mapping[str, Any] | str],
   203 |         config: ShadowConfig | None = None,
   204 |         *,
   205 |         iterations: int = 1,
   206 |     ) -> dict[str, Any]:
   207 |         """Full lifecycle: spin up shadow Docker container, run simulation, tear down."""
   208 |         shadow_instance: ShadowDatabase | None = None
   209 |         try:
   210 |             shadow_instance = await provision_shadow_db(config)
   211 |             await clone_customer_database(source_dsn, shadow_instance.dsn)
   212 |             conn = await shadow_instance.connect()
   213 |             try:
   214 |                 result = await self.run_simulation_experiment(
   215 |                     conn, candidate_sql, workload, iterations=iterations
   216 |                 )
   217 |                 result["container_id"] = shadow_instance.container_id
   218 |                 return result
   219 |             finally:
   220 |                 await conn.close()
   221 |         finally:
   222 |             if shadow_instance:
   223 |                 await teardown_shadow_db(shadow_instance.container_id)

   135 | async def collect_connection_telemetry(
   136 |     connection_id: UUID,
   137 |     customer_pool: asyncpg.Pool,
   138 |     session: AsyncSession,
   139 |     previous_tables: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
   140 |     previous_captured_at: datetime | None = None,
   141 |     max_plan_queries: int = 10,
   142 | ) -> dict[str, int]:
   143 |     """Collect and persist one snapshot for one monitored database.
   144 | 
   145 |     The customer connection is only used through fixed read-only tools. The
   146 |     application session receives one atomic batch for this customer.
   147 |     """
   148 |     captured_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   149 |     previous_tables = previous_tables if previous_tables is not None else {}
   150 |     elapsed = (captured_at - previous_captured_at).total_seconds() if previous_captured_at else None
   151 | 
   152 |     async with customer_pool.acquire() as customer:
   153 |         try:
   154 |             query_rows = await pg_introspection.get_query_metrics(customer)
   155 |         except asyncpg.PostgresError as exc:
   156 |             logger.warning("Query telemetry unavailable", extra={"connection_id": str(connection_id), "error": str(exc)})
   157 |             query_rows = []
   158 |         try:
   159 |             table_rows = await pg_introspection.get_table_stats(customer)
   160 |         except asyncpg.PostgresError as exc:
   161 |             logger.warning("Table telemetry unavailable", extra={"connection_id": str(connection_id), "error": str(exc)})
   162 |             table_rows = []
   163 | 
   164 |         query_metrics = [_query_metric(connection_id, captured_at, row) for row in query_rows]
   165 |         table_metrics = []
   166 |         for row in table_rows:
   167 |             key = (row.get("schemaname") or "public", row.get("relname") or "unknown")
   168 |             table_metrics.append(_table_metric(connection_id, captured_at, row, previous_tables.get(key), elapsed))
   169 |             previous_tables[key] = row
   170 | 
   171 |         plan_metrics: list[PlanMetric] = []
   172 |         for query_metric in query_metrics[:max(0, max_plan_queries)]:
   173 |             if not _is_plan_eligible(query_metric.query_text):
   174 |                 continue
   175 |             try:
   176 |                 features = await pg_introspection.get_query_plan(customer, query_metric.query_text or "")
   177 |             except (asyncpg.PostgresError, ValueError) as exc:
   178 |                 logger.debug(
   179 |                     "Skipping plan capture for query",
   180 |                     extra={"connection_id": str(connection_id), "query_id": query_metric.queryid, "error": str(exc)},
   181 |                 )
   182 |                 continue
   183 |             plan_metrics.append(PlanMetric(
   184 |                 id=uuid4(),
   185 |                 connection_id=connection_id,
   186 |                 query_metrics_id=query_metric.id,
   187 |                 capture_source="live_postgresql",
   188 |                 timestamp=captured_at,
   189 |                 query_id=query_metric.queryid,
   190 |                 plan_hash=_plan_hash(features),
   191 |                 node_types=features.get("node_types"),
   192 |                 estimated_rows=_float(features.get("estimated_rows")),
   193 |                 actual_rows=_float(features.get("actual_rows")),
   194 |                 estimated_cost=_float(features.get("estimated_cost")),
   195 |                 actual_time=_float(features.get("actual_time")),
   196 |                 buffer_hits=_int(features.get("buffer_hits")),
   197 |                 buffer_reads=_int(features.get("buffer_reads")),
   198 |                 join_types=features.get("join_types"),
   199 |                 parallel_workers=_int(features.get("parallel_workers")),
   200 |             ))
   201 | 
   202 |     session.add_all([*query_metrics, *table_metrics, *plan_metrics])
   203 |     await session.flush()
   204 |     return {"queries": len(query_metrics), "tables": len(table_metrics), "plans": len(plan_metrics)}

   207 | async def collect_once(
   208 |     session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession] = async_session_factory,
   209 |     connection_manager: Any = customer_connection_manager,
   210 |     previous_state: dict[UUID, tuple[datetime, dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, Any]]]] | None = None,
   211 | ) -> dict[str, int]:
   212 |     """Collect one cycle for every active customer connection."""
   213 |     previous_state = previous_state if previous_state is not None else {}
   214 |     totals = {"connections": 0, "queries": 0, "tables": 0, "plans": 0, "errors": 0}
   215 |     async with session_factory() as session:
   216 |         records = (await session.execute(
   217 |             select(DatabaseConnection).where(DatabaseConnection.is_active.is_(True))
   218 |         )).scalars().all()
   219 |         for record in records:
   220 |             totals["connections"] += 1
   221 |             previous = previous_state.get(record.id)
   222 |             try:
   223 |                 async with session.begin_nested():
   224 |                     pool = await connection_manager.get_customer_pool(record.id, db=session)
   225 |                     table_state = previous[1] if previous else {}
   226 |                     counts = await collect_connection_telemetry(
   227 |                         record.id,
   228 |                         pool,
   229 |                         session,
   230 |                         previous_tables=table_state,
   231 |                         previous_captured_at=previous[0] if previous else None,
   232 |                     )
   233 |                 captured_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   234 |                 previous_state[record.id] = (captured_at, table_state)
   235 |                 for key in ("queries", "tables", "plans"):
   236 |                     totals[key] += counts[key]
   237 |             except Exception:
   238 |                 totals["errors"] += 1
   239 |                 logger.exception("Telemetry collection failed", extra={"connection_id": str(record.id)})
   240 |         await session.commit()
   241 |     return totals

   244 | async def run_worker(
   245 |     stop_event: asyncio.Event | None = None,
   246 |     session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession] = async_session_factory,
   247 |     connection_manager: Any = customer_connection_manager,
   248 |     poll_interval: int | None = None,
   249 | ) -> None:
   250 |     """Run the collector until cancelled or the stop event is set."""
   251 |     settings = get_settings()
   252 |     interval = max(1, poll_interval or settings.TELEMETRY_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS)
   253 |     stop_event = stop_event or asyncio.Event()
   254 |     previous_state: dict[UUID, tuple[datetime, dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, Any]]]] = {}
   255 |     while not stop_event.is_set():
   256 |         await collect_once(session_factory, connection_manager, previous_state)
   257 |         try:
   258 |             await asyncio.wait_for(stop_event.wait(), timeout=interval)
   259 |         except asyncio.TimeoutError:
   260 |             continue

    37 | // All coordinates are percentages of the snapshot reference box: Chrome 150
    38 | // renders absolute px clip-path coordinates on ::view-transition-new(root)
